/**
   * Defines a property whose type is inferred.
   * @param propertyName the property's name
   * @param type the type
   * @param propertyNode the node corresponding to the inferred definition of
   *        property that might later be accessed using {@code getPropertyNode}.
   */
Method code:
312 |   public final boolean defineInferredProperty(String propertyName,
313 |       JSType type, Node propertyNode) {
314 |     StaticSlot<JSType> originalSlot = getSlot(propertyName);
315 |     if (hasProperty(propertyName)) {
316 |       if (isPropertyTypeDeclared(propertyName)) {
317 |         // We never want to hide a declared property with an inferred property.
318 |         return true;
319 |       }
320 |       JSType originalType = getPropertyType(propertyName);
321 |       type = originalType == null ? type :
322 |           originalType.getLeastSupertype(type);
323 |     }
324 | 
325 |     boolean result = defineProperty(propertyName, type, true,
326 |         propertyNode);
327 | 
328 |     // All property definitions go through this method
329 |     // or defineDeclaredProperty. Because the properties defined an an
330 |     // object can affect subtyping, it's slightly more efficient
331 |     // to register this after defining the property.
332 |     registry.registerPropertyOnType(propertyName, this);
333 | 
334 |     return result;
335 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CodePrinter.CompactCodePrinter.maybeLineBreak()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CodePrinter.java
Original range: 464-484
Documentation:

Method code:
464 |     @Override
465 |     void maybeLineBreak() {
466 |       if (lineBreak) {
467 |         if (sawFunction) {
468 |           startNewLine();
469 |           sawFunction = false;
470 |         }
471 |       }
472 | 
473 |       // Since we are at a legal line break, can we upgrade the
474 |       // preferred break position?  We prefer to break after a
475 |       // semicolon rather than before it.
476 |       int len = code.length();
477 |       if (preferredBreakPosition == len - 1) {
478 |         char ch = code.charAt(len - 1);
479 |         if (ch == ';') {
480 |           preferredBreakPosition = len;
481 |         }
482 |       }
483 |       maybeCutLine();
484 |     }

203 |   private boolean isConnectedInDirection(N n1, Predicate<E> edgeMatcher, N n2) {

1249 |     private void finishConstructorDefinition(
1250 |         Node n, String variableName, FunctionType fnType,
1251 |         Scope scopeToDeclareIn, CompilerInput input, Var newVar) {
1252 |       // Declare var.prototype in the scope chain.
1253 |       FunctionType superClassCtor = fnType.getSuperClassConstructor();
1254 |       Property prototypeSlot = fnType.getSlot("prototype");
1255 | 
1256 |       // When we declare the function prototype implicitly, we
1257 |       // want to make sure that the function and its prototype
1258 |       // are declared at the same node. We also want to make sure
1259 |       // that the if a symbol has both a Var and a JSType, they have
1260 |       // the same node.
1261 |       //
1262 |       // This consistency is helpful to users of SymbolTable,
1263 |       // because everything gets declared at the same place.
1264 |       prototypeSlot.setNode(n);
1265 | 
1266 |       String prototypeName = variableName + ".prototype";
1267 | 
1268 |       // There are some rare cases where the prototype will already
1269 |       // be declared. See TypedScopeCreatorTest#testBogusPrototypeInit.
1270 |       // Fortunately, other warnings will complain if this happens.
1271 |       Var prototypeVar = scopeToDeclareIn.getVar(prototypeName);
1272 |       if (prototypeVar != null && prototypeVar.scope == scopeToDeclareIn) {
1273 |         scopeToDeclareIn.undeclare(prototypeVar);
1274 |       }
1275 | 
1276 |       scopeToDeclareIn.declare(prototypeName,
1277 |           n, prototypeSlot.getType(), input,
1278 |           /* declared iff there's an explicit supertype */
1279 |           superClassCtor == null ||
1280 |           superClassCtor.getInstanceType().isEquivalentTo(
1281 |               getNativeType(OBJECT_TYPE)));
1282 | 
1283 |       // Make sure the variable is initialized to something if
1284 |       // it constructs itself.
1285 |       if (newVar.getInitialValue() == null &&
1286 |           !n.isFromExterns()) {
1287 |         compiler.report(
1288 |             JSError.make(sourceName, n,

/**
   * Computes the destination node of n when we want to fallthrough into the
   * subtree of n. We don't always create a CFG edge into n itself because of
   * DOs and FORs.
   */
Method code:
796 |   static Node computeFallThrough(Node n) {
797 |     switch (n.getType()) {
798 |       case Token.DO:

807 |       default:

809 |     }
810 |   }

===== M0085 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowGraph.isEnteringNewCfgNode(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowGraph.java
Original range: 159-205
Documentation:
/**
   * @return True if n should be represented by a new CFG node in the control
   * flow graph.
   */
Method code:
159 |   public static boolean isEnteringNewCfgNode(Node n) {
160 |     Node parent = n.getParent();
161 |     switch (parent.getType()) {
162 |       case Token.BLOCK:
163 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
164 |       case Token.TRY:
165 |         return true;
166 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
167 |         // A function node represents the start of a function where the name
168 |         // bleeds into the local scope and parameters are assigned
169 |         // to the formal argument names. The node includes the name of the
170 |         // function and the LP list since we assume the whole set up process
171 |         // is atomic without change in control flow. The next change of
172 |         // control is going into the function's body, represented by the second
173 |         // child.
174 |         return n != parent.getFirstChild().getNext();
175 |       case Token.WHILE:
176 |       case Token.DO:
177 |       case Token.IF:
178 |         // These control structures are represented by a node that holds the
179 |         // condition. Each of them is a branch node based on its condition.
180 |         return NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(parent) != n;
181 | 
182 |       case Token.FOR:
183 |         // The FOR(;;) node differs from other control structures in that
184 |         // it has an initialization and an increment statement. Those
185 |         // two statements have corresponding CFG nodes to represent them.
186 |         // The FOR node only represents the condition check for each iteration.
187 |         // That way the following:
188 |         // for(var x = 0; x < 10; x++) { } has a graph that is isomorphic to
189 |         // var x = 0; while(x<10) {  x++; }
190 |         if (NodeUtil.isForIn(parent)) {
191 |           // TODO(user): Investigate how we should handle the case where
192 |           // we have a very complex expression inside the FOR-IN header.
193 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
194 |         } else {
195 |           return NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(parent) != n;
196 |         }
197 |       case Token.SWITCH:
198 |       case Token.CASE:
199 |       case Token.CATCH:
200 |       case Token.WITH:
201 |         return n != parent.getFirstChild();
202 |       default:
203 |         return false;
204 |     }
205 |   }

===== M0127 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.InferJSDocInfo.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/InferJSDocInfo.java
Original range: 92-189
Documentation:

Method code:
92 |   @Override
93 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
94 |     JSDocInfo docInfo;
95 | 
96 |     switch (n.getType()) {
97 |       // Infer JSDocInfo on types of all type declarations on variables.
98 |       case Token.NAME:
99 |         if (parent == null) {
100 |           return;
101 |         }
102 | 
103 |         // Only allow JSDoc on VARs, function declarations, and assigns.
104 |         if (!parent.isVar() &&
105 |             !NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(parent) &&
106 |             !(parent.isAssign() &&
107 |               n == parent.getFirstChild())) {
108 |           return;
109 |         }
110 | 
111 |         // There are four places the doc info could live.
112 |         // 1) A FUNCTION node.
113 |         // /** ... */ function f() { ... }
114 |         // 2) An ASSIGN parent.
115 |         // /** ... */ x = function () { ... }
116 |         // 3) A NAME parent.
117 |         // var x, /** ... */ y = function() { ... }
118 |         // 4) A VAR gramps.
119 |         // /** ... */ var x = function() { ... }
120 |         docInfo = n.getJSDocInfo();
121 |         if (docInfo == null &&
122 |             !(parent.isVar() &&
123 |                 !parent.hasOneChild())) {
124 |           docInfo = parent.getJSDocInfo();
125 |         }
126 | 
127 |         // Try to find the type of the NAME.
128 |         JSType varType = n.getJSType();
129 |         if (varType == null && parent.isFunction()) {
130 |           varType = parent.getJSType();
131 |         }
132 | 
133 |         // If we have no type to attach JSDocInfo to, then there's nothing
134 |         // we can do.
135 |         if (varType == null || docInfo == null) {
136 |           return;
137 |         }
138 | 
139 |         // Dereference the type. If the result is not an object, or already
140 |         // has docs attached, then do nothing.
141 |         ObjectType objType = dereferenceToObject(varType);
142 |         if (objType == null || objType.getJSDocInfo() != null) {
143 |           return;
144 |         }
145 | 
146 |         attachJSDocInfoToNominalTypeOrShape(objType, docInfo, n.getString());
147 |         break;
148 | 
149 |       case Token.GETPROP:
150 |         // Infer JSDocInfo on properties.
151 |         // There are two ways to write doc comments on a property.
152 |         //
153 |         // 1)
154 |         // /** @deprecated */
155 |         // obj.prop = ...
156 |         //
157 |         // 2)
158 |         // /** @deprecated */
159 |         // obj.prop;
160 |         if (parent.isExprResult() ||
161 |             (parent.isAssign() &&
162 |              parent.getFirstChild() == n)) {
163 |           docInfo = n.getJSDocInfo();
164 |           if (docInfo == null) {
165 |             docInfo = parent.getJSDocInfo();
166 |           }
167 |           if (docInfo != null) {
168 |             ObjectType lhsType =
169 |                 dereferenceToObject(n.getFirstChild().getJSType());
170 |             if (lhsType != null) {
171 |               // Put the JSDoc in the property slot, if there is one.
172 |               String propName = n.getLastChild().getString();
173 |               if (lhsType.hasOwnProperty(propName)) {
174 |                 lhsType.setPropertyJSDocInfo(propName, docInfo);
175 |               }
176 | 
177 |               // Put the JSDoc in any constructors or function shapes as well.
178 |               ObjectType propType =
179 |                   dereferenceToObject(lhsType.getPropertyType(propName));
180 |               if (propType != null) {
181 |                 attachJSDocInfoToNominalTypeOrShape(
182 |                     propType, docInfo, n.getQualifiedName());
183 |               }
184 |             }
185 |           }
186 |         }
187 |         break;
188 |     }
189 |   }

1597 |   private JSType createFromTypeNodesInternal(Node n, String sourceName,
1598 |       StaticScope<JSType> scope) {
1599 |     switch (n.getType()) {
1600 |       case Token.LC: // Record type.
1601 |         return createRecordTypeFromNodes(
1602 |             n.getFirstChild(), sourceName, scope);
1603 | 
1604 |       case Token.BANG: // Not nullable
1605 |         return createFromTypeNodesInternal(
1606 |             n.getFirstChild(), sourceName, scope)
1607 |             .restrictByNotNullOrUndefined();
1608 | 
1609 |       case Token.QMARK: // Nullable or unknown
1610 |         Node firstChild = n.getFirstChild();
1611 |         if (firstChild == null) {
1612 |           return getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE);
1613 |         }
1614 |         return createDefaultObjectUnion(
1615 |             createFromTypeNodesInternal(
1616 |                 firstChild, sourceName, scope));
1617 | 
1618 |       case Token.EQUALS: // Optional
1619 |         return createOptionalType(
1620 |             createFromTypeNodesInternal(
1621 |                 n.getFirstChild(), sourceName, scope));
1622 | 
1623 |       case Token.ELLIPSIS: // Var args
1624 |         return createOptionalType(
1625 |             createFromTypeNodesInternal(
1626 |                 n.getFirstChild(), sourceName, scope));
1627 | 
1628 |       case Token.STAR: // The AllType
1629 |         return getNativeType(ALL_TYPE);
1630 | 
1631 |       case Token.LB: // Array type
1632 |         // TODO(nicksantos): Enforce membership restrictions on the Array.
1633 |         return getNativeType(ARRAY_TYPE);
1634 | 
1635 |       case Token.PIPE: // Union type
1636 |         UnionTypeBuilder builder = new UnionTypeBuilder(this);
1637 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild(); child != null;
1638 |              child = child.getNext()) {
1639 |           builder.addAlternate(
1640 |               createFromTypeNodesInternal(child, sourceName, scope));
1641 |         }
1642 |         return builder.build();
1643 | 
1644 |       case Token.EMPTY: // When the return value of a function is not specified
1645 |         return getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE);
1646 | 
1647 |       case Token.VOID: // Only allowed in the return value of a function.
1648 |         return getNativeType(VOID_TYPE);
1649 | 
1650 |       case Token.STRING:
1651 |         JSType namedType = getType(scope, n.getString(), sourceName,
1652 |             n.getLineno(), n.getCharno());
1653 |         if ((namedType instanceof ObjectType) &&
1654 |             !(namedType instanceof NamespaceType) &&
1655 |             !(nonNullableTypeNames.contains(n.getString()))) {
1656 |           Node typeList = n.getFirstChild();
1657 |           int nAllowedTypes =
1658 |               namedType.getTemplateTypeMap().numUnfilledTemplateKeys();
1659 |           if (typeList != null && nAllowedTypes > 0) {
1660 |             // Templatized types.
1661 |             ImmutableList.Builder<JSType> templateTypes =
1662 |                 ImmutableList.builder();
1663 | 
1664 |             // Special case for Object, where Object.<X> implies Object.<?,X>.
1665 |             if (n.getString().equals("Object") &&
1666 |                 typeList.getFirstChild() == typeList.getLastChild()) {
1667 |               templateTypes.add(getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE));
1668 |             }
1669 | 
1670 |             int templateNodeIndex = 0;
1671 |             for (Node templateNode : typeList.getFirstChild().siblings()) {
1672 |               // Don't parse more templatized type nodes than the type can
1673 |               // accommodate. This is because some existing clients have
1674 |               // template annotations on non-templatized classes, for instance:
1675 |               //   goog.structs.Set.<SomeType>
1676 |               // The problem in these cases is that the previously-unparsed
1677 |               // SomeType is not actually a valid type. To prevent these clients
1678 |               // from seeing unknown type errors, we explicitly don't parse
1679 |               // these types.
1680 |               // TODO(user): Address this issue by removing bad template
1681 |               // annotations on non-templatized classes.
1682 |               if (++templateNodeIndex > nAllowedTypes) {
1683 |                 break;
1684 |               }
1685 |               templateTypes.add(createFromTypeNodesInternal(
1686 |                   templateNode, sourceName, scope));
1687 |             }
1688 |             namedType = createTemplatizedType(
1689 |                 (ObjectType) namedType, templateTypes.build());
1690 |             Preconditions.checkNotNull(namedType);
1691 |           }
1692 |           return createDefaultObjectUnion(namedType);
1693 |         } else {
1694 |           return namedType;
1695 |         }
1696 | 
1697 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
1698 |         ObjectType thisType = null;
1699 |         boolean isConstructor = false;
1700 |         Node current = n.getFirstChild();
1701 |         if (current.getType() == Token.THIS ||
1702 |             current.getType() == Token.NEW) {
1703 |           Node contextNode = current.getFirstChild();
1704 |           thisType =
1705 |               ObjectType.cast(
1706 |                   createFromTypeNodesInternal(
1707 |                       contextNode, sourceName, scope)
1708 |                   .restrictByNotNullOrUndefined());
1709 |           if (thisType == null) {
1710 |             reporter.warning(
1711 |                 SimpleErrorReporter.getMessage0(
1712 |                     current.getType() == Token.THIS ?
1713 |                     "msg.jsdoc.function.thisnotobject" :
1714 |                     "msg.jsdoc.function.newnotobject"),
1715 |                 sourceName,
1716 |                 contextNode.getLineno(), contextNode.getCharno());
1717 |           }
1718 | 
1719 |           isConstructor = current.getType() == Token.NEW;
1720 |           current = current.getNext();
1721 |         }
1722 | 
1723 |         FunctionParamBuilder paramBuilder = new FunctionParamBuilder(this);
1724 | 
1725 |         if (current.getType() == Token.PARAM_LIST) {
1726 |           for (Node arg = current.getFirstChild(); arg != null;
1727 |                arg = arg.getNext()) {
1728 |             if (arg.getType() == Token.ELLIPSIS) {
1729 |               if (arg.getChildCount() == 0) {
1730 |                 paramBuilder.addVarArgs(getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE));
1731 |               } else {
1732 |                 paramBuilder.addVarArgs(
1733 |                     createFromTypeNodesInternal(
1734 |                         arg.getFirstChild(), sourceName, scope));
1735 |               }
1736 |             } else {
1737 |               JSType type = createFromTypeNodesInternal(
1738 |                   arg, sourceName, scope);
1739 |               if (arg.getType() == Token.EQUALS) {
1740 |                 boolean addSuccess = paramBuilder.addOptionalParams(type);
1741 |                 if (!addSuccess) {
1742 |                   reporter.warning(
1743 |                       SimpleErrorReporter.getMessage0(
1744 |                           "msg.jsdoc.function.varargs"),
1745 |                       sourceName, arg.getLineno(), arg.getCharno());
1746 |                 }
1747 |               } else {
1748 |                 paramBuilder.addRequiredParams(type);
1749 |               }
1750 |             }
1751 |           }
1752 |           current = current.getNext();
1753 |         }
1754 | 
1755 |         JSType returnType =
1756 |             createFromTypeNodesInternal(current, sourceName, scope);
1757 | 
1758 |         return new FunctionBuilder(this)
1759 |             .withParams(paramBuilder)
1760 |             .withReturnType(returnType)
1761 |             .withTypeOfThis(thisType)
1762 |             .setIsConstructor(isConstructor)
1763 |             .build();
1764 |     }
1765 |

1768 |   }

1001 |   private String jsString(String s, boolean useSlashV) {
1002 |     int singleq = 0, doubleq = 0;
1003 | 
1004 |     // could count the quotes and pick the optimal quote character
1005 |     for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {
1006 |       switch (s.charAt(i)) {
1007 |         case '"': doubleq++; break;

1015 |         (singleq <= doubleq) : (singleq < doubleq)) {

1017 |       quote = '\'';

1019 |       singlequote = "\\\'";
1020 |     } else {
1021 |       // more single quotes so escape the doubles
1022 |       quote = '\"';
1023 |       doublequote = "\\\"";
1024 |       singlequote = "\'";
1025 |     }
1026 |

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.parsing.IRFactory.validateTypeAnnotations(JSDocInfo,AstNode)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/parsing/IRFactory.java
Original range: 295-354
Documentation:

Method code:
295 |   private void validateTypeAnnotations(JSDocInfo info, AstNode node) {
296 |     if (info.hasType()) {
297 |       boolean valid = false;
298 |       switch (node.getType()) {
299 |         // Casts are valid
300 |         case com.google.javascript.rhino.head.Token.LP:
301 |           valid = node instanceof ParenthesizedExpression;
302 |           break;
303 |         // Variable declarations are valid
304 |         case com.google.javascript.rhino.head.Token.VAR:
305 |           valid = true;
306 |           break;
307 |         // Function declarations are valid
308 |         case com.google.javascript.rhino.head.Token.FUNCTION:
309 |           FunctionNode fnNode = (FunctionNode) node;
310 |           valid = fnNode.getFunctionType() == FunctionNode.FUNCTION_STATEMENT;
311 |           break;
312 |         // Object literal properties, catch declarations and variable
313 |         // initializers are valid.
314 |         case com.google.javascript.rhino.head.Token.NAME:
315 |           AstNode parent = node.getParent();
316 |           valid = parent instanceof ObjectProperty
317 |               || parent instanceof CatchClause
318 |               || parent instanceof FunctionNode
319 |               || (parent instanceof VariableInitializer &&
320 |                   node == ((VariableInitializer) parent).getTarget());
321 |           break;
322 |         // Object literal properties are valid
323 |         case com.google.javascript.rhino.head.Token.GET:
324 |         case com.google.javascript.rhino.head.Token.SET:
325 |         case com.google.javascript.rhino.head.Token.NUMBER:
326 |         case com.google.javascript.rhino.head.Token.STRING:
327 |           valid = node.getParent() instanceof ObjectProperty;
328 |           break;
329 | 
330 |         // Property assignments are valid, if at the root of an expression.
331 |         case com.google.javascript.rhino.head.Token.ASSIGN:
332 |           if (node instanceof Assignment) {
333 |             valid = isExprStmt(node.getParent())
334 |                 && isPropAccess(((Assignment) node).getLeft());
335 |           }
336 |           break;
337 | 
338 |         // Property definitions are valid, if at the root of an expression.
339 |         case com.google.javascript.rhino.head.Token.GETPROP:
340 |         case com.google.javascript.rhino.head.Token.GETELEM:
341 |           valid = isExprStmt(node.getParent());
342 |           break;
343 | 
344 |         case com.google.javascript.rhino.head.Token.CALL:
345 |           valid = info.isDefine();
346 |           break;
347 |       }
348 |       if (!valid) {
349 |         errorReporter.warning(MISPLACED_TYPE_ANNOTATION,
350 |             sourceName,
351 |             node.getLineno(), "", 0);
352 |       }
353 |     }
354 |   }

===== M0177 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.process(Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 148-190
Documentation:

Method code:
148 |   @Override
149 |   public void process(Node externs, Node root) {
150 |     this.root = root;
151 |     astPositionCounter = 0;
152 |     astPosition = Maps.newHashMap();
153 |     nodePriorities = Maps.newHashMap();
154 |     cfg = new AstControlFlowGraph(computeFallThrough(root), nodePriorities,
155 |                                   edgeAnnotations);
156 |     NodeTraversal.traverse(compiler, root, this);
157 |     astPosition.put(null, ++astPositionCounter); // the implicit return is last.
158 | 
159 |     // Now, generate the priority of nodes by doing a depth-first
160 |     // search on the CFG.
161 |     priorityCounter = 0;
162 |     DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> entry = cfg.getEntry();
163 |     prioritizeFromEntryNode(entry);
164 | 
165 |     if (shouldTraverseFunctions) {
166 |       // If we're traversing inner functions, we need to rank the
167 |       // priority of them too.
168 |       for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> candidate : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
169 |         Node value = candidate.getValue();
170 |         if (value != null && value.isFunction()) {
171 |           Preconditions.checkState(
172 |               !nodePriorities.containsKey(candidate) || candidate == entry);
173 |           prioritizeFromEntryNode(candidate);
174 |         }
175 |       }
176 |     }
177 | 
178 |     // At this point, all reachable nodes have been given a priority, but
179 |     // unreachable nodes have not been given a priority. Put them last.
180 |     // Presumably, it doesn't really matter what priority they get, since
181 |     // this shouldn't happen in real code.
182 |     for (DiGraphNode<Node, Branch> candidate : cfg.getDirectedGraphNodes()) {
183 |       if (!nodePriorities.containsKey(candidate)) {
184 |         nodePriorities.put(candidate, ++priorityCounter);
185 |       }
186 |     }
187 | 
188 |     // Again, the implicit return node is always last.
189 |     nodePriorities.put(cfg.getImplicitReturn(), ++priorityCounter);
190 |   }

   * Visits an object literal field definition <code>key : value</code>.
   *
   * If the <code>lvalue</code> is a prototype modification, we change the

   *

Method code:
1073 |   private void visitObjLitKey(
1074 |       NodeTraversal t, Node key, Node objlit, JSType litType) {
1075 |     // Do not validate object lit value types in externs. We don't really care,
1076 |     // and it makes it easier to generate externs.
1077 |     if (objlit.isFromExterns()) {
1078 |       ensureTyped(t, key);
1079 |       return;
1080 |     }
1081 | 
1082 |     // Structs must have unquoted keys and dicts must have quoted keys
1083 |     if (litType.isStruct() && key.isQuotedString()) {
1084 |       report(t, key, ILLEGAL_OBJLIT_KEY, "struct");
1085 |     } else if (litType.isDict() && !key.isQuotedString()) {
1086 |       report(t, key, ILLEGAL_OBJLIT_KEY, "dict");
1087 |     }
1088 | 
1089 |     // TODO(johnlenz): Validate get and set function declarations are valid
1090 |     // as is the functions can have "extraneous" bits.
1091 | 
1092 |     // For getter and setter property definitions the
1093 |     // r-value type != the property type.
1094 |     Node rvalue = key.getFirstChild();
1095 |     JSType rightType = NodeUtil.getObjectLitKeyTypeFromValueType(
1096 |         key, getJSType(rvalue));
1097 |     if (rightType == null) {
1098 |       rightType = getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE);
1099 |     }
1100 | 
1101 |     Node owner = objlit;
1102 | 
1103 |     // Validate value is assignable to the key type.
1104 | 
1105 |     JSType keyType = getJSType(key);
1106 | 
1107 |     JSType allowedValueType = keyType;
1108 |     if (allowedValueType.isEnumElementType()) {
1109 |       allowedValueType =
1110 |           allowedValueType.toMaybeEnumElementType().getPrimitiveType();
1111 |     }
1112 | 
1113 |     boolean valid = validator.expectCanAssignToPropertyOf(t, key,
1114 |         rightType, allowedValueType,
1115 |         owner, NodeUtil.getObjectLitKeyName(key));
1116 |     if (valid) {
1117 |       ensureTyped(t, key, rightType);
1118 |     } else {
1119 |       ensureTyped(t, key);
1120 |     }
1121 | 
1122 |     // Validate that the key type is assignable to the object property type.
1123 |     // This is necessary as the objlit may have been cast to a non-literal
1124 |     // object type.
1125 |     // TODO(johnlenz): consider introducing a CAST node to the AST (or
1126 |     // perhaps a parentheses node).
1127 | 
1128 |     JSType objlitType = getJSType(objlit);
1129 |     ObjectType type = ObjectType.cast(
1130 |         objlitType.restrictByNotNullOrUndefined());

1133 |       if (type.hasProperty(property) &&
1134 |           !type.isPropertyTypeInferred(property) &&
1135 |           !propertyIsImplicitCast(type, property)) {

258 |   @Override
259 |   public boolean equals(Object other) {
260 |     if (other instanceof LinkedFlowScope) {
261 |       LinkedFlowScope that = (LinkedFlowScope) other;
262 |       if (this.optimize() == that.optimize()) {
263 |         return true;
264 |       }
265 | 
266 |       // If two flow scopes are in the same function, then they could have
267 |       // two possible function scopes: the real one and the BOTTOM scope.
268 |       // If they have different function scopes, we *should* iterate through all
269 |       // the variables in each scope and compare. However, 99.9% of the time,
270 |       // they're not equal. And the other .1% of the time, we can pretend
271 |       // they're equal--this just means that data flow analysis will have
272 |       // to propagate the entry lattice a little bit further than it
273 |       // really needs to. Everything will still come out ok.
274 |       if (this.getFunctionScope() != that.getFunctionScope()) {
275 |         return false;
276 |       }
277 | 
278 |       if (cache == that.cache) {
279 |         // If the two flow scopes have the same cache, then we can check
280 |         // equality a lot faster: by just looking at the "dirty" elements
281 |         // in the cache, and comparing them in both scopes.
282 |         for (String name : cache.dirtySymbols) {
283 |           if (diffSlots(getSlot(name), that.getSlot(name))) {
284 |             return false;
285 |           }
286 |         }
287 | 
288 |         return true;
289 |       }
290 | 
291 |       Map<String, StaticSlot<JSType>> myFlowSlots = allFlowSlots();
292 |       Map<String, StaticSlot<JSType>> otherFlowSlots = that.allFlowSlots();
293 | 
294 |       for (StaticSlot<JSType> slot : myFlowSlots.values()) {
295 |         if (diffSlots(slot, otherFlowSlots.get(slot.getName()))) {
296 |           return false;
297 |         }
298 |         otherFlowSlots.remove(slot.getName());
299 |       }
300 |       for (StaticSlot<JSType> slot : otherFlowSlots.values()) {
301 |         if (diffSlots(slot, myFlowSlots.get(slot.getName()))) {
302 |           return false;
303 |         }
304 |       }
305 |       return true;
306 |     }
307 |     return false;
308 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.JSType.isSubtypeHelper(JSType,JSType)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/rhino/jstype/JSType.java
Original range: 1236-1296
Documentation:
/**
   * A generic implementation meant to be used as a helper for common subtyping
   * cases.
   */
Method code:
1236 |   static boolean isSubtypeHelper(JSType thisType, JSType thatType) {
1237 |     // unknown
1238 |     if (thatType.isUnknownType()) {
1239 |       return true;
1240 |     }
1241 |     // all type
1242 |     if (thatType.isAllType()) {
1243 |       return true;
1244 |     }
1245 |     // equality
1246 |     if (thisType.isEquivalentTo(thatType)) {
1247 |       return true;
1248 |     }
1249 |     // unions
1250 |     if (thatType.isUnionType()) {
1251 |       UnionType union = thatType.toMaybeUnionType();
1252 |       for (JSType element : union.alternates) {
1253 |         if (thisType.isSubtype(element)) {
1254 |           return true;
1255 |         }
1256 |       }
1257 |       return false;
1258 |     }
1259 | 
1260 |     // TemplateTypeMaps. This check only returns false if the TemplateTypeMaps
1261 |     // are not equivalent.
1262 |     TemplateTypeMap thisTypeParams = thisType.getTemplateTypeMap();
1263 |     TemplateTypeMap thatTypeParams = thatType.getTemplateTypeMap();
1264 |     boolean templateMatch = true;
1265 |     if (isExemptFromTemplateTypeInvariance(thatType)) {
1266 |       // Array and Object are exempt from template type invariance; their
1267 |       // template types maps are considered a match only if the ObjectElementKey
1268 |       // values are subtypes/supertypes of one another.
1269 |       TemplateType key = thisType.registry.getObjectElementKey();
1270 |       JSType thisElement = thisTypeParams.getTemplateType(key);
1271 |       JSType thatElement = thatTypeParams.getTemplateType(key);
1272 | 
1273 |       templateMatch = thisElement.isSubtype(thatElement)
1274 |           || thatElement.isSubtype(thisElement);
1275 |     } else {
1276 |       templateMatch = thisTypeParams.checkEquivalenceHelper(
1277 |           thatTypeParams, EquivalenceMethod.INVARIANT);
1278 |     }
1279 |     if (!templateMatch) {
1280 |       return false;
1281 |     }
1282 | 
1283 |     // Templatized types. The above check guarantees TemplateTypeMap
1284 |     // equivalence; check if the base type is a subtype.
1285 |     if (thisType.isTemplatizedType()) {
1286 |       return thisType.toMaybeTemplatizedType().getReferencedType().isSubtype(
1287 |               thatType);
1288 |     }
1289 | 
1290 |     // proxy types
1291 |     if (thatType instanceof ProxyObjectType) {
1292 |       return thisType.isSubtype(
1293 |           ((ProxyObjectType) thatType).getReferencedTypeInternal());
1294 |     }
1295 |     return false;
1296 |   }

/**
   * Look ahead for a type annotation by advancing the character stream.
   * Does not modify the token stream.
   * This is kind of a hack, and is only necessary because we use the token
   * stream to parse types, but need the underlying character stream to get
   * JsDoc descriptions.

2506 |       } else {

2508 |       }
2509 |     }

2511 |     return matchedLc;

===== M0254 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeInference.getPropertyType(JSType,String,Node,FlowScope)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/TypeInference.java
Original range: 1315-1376
Documentation:

Method code:
1315 |   private JSType getPropertyType(JSType objType, String propName,
1316 |       Node n, FlowScope scope) {
1317 |     // We often have a couple of different types to choose from for the
1318 |     // property. Ordered by accuracy, we have
1319 |     // 1) A locally inferred qualified name (which is in the FlowScope)
1320 |     // 2) A globally declared qualified name (which is in the FlowScope)
1321 |     // 3) A property on the owner type (which is on objType)
1322 |     // 4) A name in the type registry (as a last resort)
1323 |     JSType propertyType = null;
1324 |     boolean isLocallyInferred = false;
1325 | 
1326 |     // Scopes sometimes contain inferred type info about qualified names.
1327 |     String qualifiedName = n.getQualifiedName();
1328 |     StaticSlot<JSType> var = scope.getSlot(qualifiedName);
1329 |     if (var != null) {
1330 |       JSType varType = var.getType();
1331 |       if (varType != null) {
1332 |         boolean isDeclared = !var.isTypeInferred();
1333 |         isLocallyInferred = (var != syntacticScope.getSlot(qualifiedName));
1334 |         if (isDeclared || isLocallyInferred) {
1335 |           propertyType = varType;
1336 |         }
1337 |       }
1338 |     }
1339 | 
1340 |     if (propertyType == null && objType != null) {
1341 |       JSType foundType = objType.findPropertyType(propName);
1342 |       if (foundType != null) {
1343 |         propertyType = foundType;
1344 |       }
1345 |     }
1346 | 
1347 |     if (propertyType != null && objType != null) {
1348 |       JSType restrictedObjType = objType.restrictByNotNullOrUndefined();
1349 |       if (restrictedObjType.isTemplatizedType()
1350 |           && propertyType.hasAnyTemplateTypes()) {
1351 |         TemplateTypeMap typeMap = restrictedObjType.getTemplateTypeMap();
1352 |         TemplateTypeMapReplacer replacer = new TemplateTypeMapReplacer(
1353 |             registry, typeMap);
1354 |         propertyType = propertyType.visit(replacer);
1355 |       }
1356 |     }
1357 | 
1358 |     if ((propertyType == null || propertyType.isUnknownType())
1359 |         && qualifiedName != null) {
1360 |       // If we find this node in the registry, then we can infer its type.
1361 |       ObjectType regType = ObjectType.cast(registry.getType(qualifiedName));
1362 |       if (regType != null) {
1363 |         propertyType = regType.getConstructor();
1364 |       }
1365 |     }
1366 | 
1367 |     if (propertyType == null) {
1368 |       return unknownType;
1369 |     } else if (propertyType.isEquivalentTo(unknownType) && isLocallyInferred) {
1370 |       // If the type has been checked in this scope,
1371 |       // then use CHECKED_UNKNOWN_TYPE instead to indicate that.
1372 |       return getNativeType(CHECKED_UNKNOWN_TYPE);
1373 |     } else {
1374 |       return propertyType;
1375 |     }
1376 |   }

/**
     * Parse the directives, encode them in the AST, and remove their nodes.
     *
     * For information on ES5 directives, see section 14.1 of
     * ECMA-262, Edition 5.
     *
     * It would be nice if Rhino would eventually take care of this for
     * us, but right now their directive-processing is a one-off.
     */
Method code:
609 |     private void parseDirectives(Node node) {

613 |         String directive = node.removeFirstChild().getFirstChild().getString();
614 |         if (directives == null) {
615 |           directives = Sets.newHashSet(directive);
616 |         } else {
617 |           directives.add(directive);
618 |         }
619 |       }
620 | 
621 |       if (directives != null) {
622 |         node.setDirectives(directives);
623 |       }
624 |     }

/**
   * Visits a NAME node.
   *
   * @param t The node traversal object that supplies context, such as the
   * scope chain to use in name lookups as well as error reporting.
   * @param n The node being visited.
   * @param parent The parent of the node n.
   * @return whether the node is typeable or not
   */
Method code:
1365 |   boolean visitName(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
1366 |     // At this stage, we need to determine whether this is a leaf
1367 |     // node in an expression (which therefore needs to have a type
1368 |     // assigned for it) versus some other decorative node that we
1369 |     // can safely ignore.  Function names, arguments (children of LP nodes) and
1370 |     // variable declarations are ignored.
1371 |     // TODO(user): remove this short-circuiting in favor of a
1372 |     // pre order traversal of the FUNCTION, CATCH, LP and VAR nodes.
1373 |     int parentNodeType = parent.getType();
1374 |     if (parentNodeType == Token.FUNCTION ||
1375 |         parentNodeType == Token.CATCH ||
1376 |         parentNodeType == Token.PARAM_LIST ||
1377 |         parentNodeType == Token.VAR) {
1378 |       return false;
1379 |     }
1380 | 
1381 |     JSType type = n.getJSType();
1382 |     if (type == null) {
1383 |       type = getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE);
1384 |       Var var = t.getScope().getVar(n.getString());
1385 |       if (var != null) {
1386 |         JSType varType = var.getType();
1387 |         if (varType != null) {
1388 |           type = varType;
1389 |         }
1390 |       }
1391 |     }
1392 |     ensureTyped(t, n, type);
1393 |     return true;
1394 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.FunctionType.setPrototypeBasedOn(ObjectType,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/rhino/jstype/FunctionType.java

Method code:
399 |   void setPrototypeBasedOn(ObjectType baseType, Node propertyNode) {
400 |     // This is a bit weird. We need to successfully handle these
401 |     // two cases:
402 |     // Foo.prototype = new Bar();
403 |     // and
404 |     // Foo.prototype = {baz: 3};
405 |     // In the first case, we do not want new properties to get
406 |     // added to Bar. In the second case, we do want new properties
407 |     // to get added to the type of the anonymous object.
408 |     //
409 |     // We handle this by breaking it into two cases:
410 |     //
411 |     // In the first case, we create a new PrototypeObjectType and set
412 |     // its implicit prototype to the type being assigned. This ensures
413 |     // that Bar will not get any properties of Foo.prototype, but properties
414 |     // later assigned to Bar will get inherited properly.
415 |     //
416 |     // In the second case, we just use the anonymous object as the prototype.
417 |     if (baseType.hasReferenceName() ||
418 |         isNativeObjectType() ||
419 |         baseType.isFunctionPrototypeType()) {
420 |       baseType = new PrototypeObjectType(
421 |           registry, getReferenceName() + ".prototype", baseType);
422 |     }
423 |     setPrototype(baseType, propertyNode);
424 |   }

===== M0291 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeCheck.visit(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/TypeCheck.java
Original range: 495-876
Documentation:
/**
   * This is the meat of the type checking.  It is basically one big switch,
   * with each case representing one type of parse tree node.  The individual
   * cases are usually pretty straightforward.
   *
   * @param t The node traversal object that supplies context, such as the
   * scope chain to use in name lookups as well as error reporting.
   * @param n The node being visited.
   * @param parent The parent of the node n.
   */
Method code:
495 |   @Override
496 |   public void visit(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
497 |     JSType childType;
498 |     JSType leftType, rightType;
499 |     Node left, right;
500 |     // To be explicitly set to false if the node is not typeable.
501 |     boolean typeable = true;
502 | 
503 |     switch (n.getType()) {
504 |       case Token.CAST:
505 |         Node expr = n.getFirstChild();
506 |         JSType exprType = getJSType(expr);
507 |         JSType castType = getJSType(n);
508 | 
509 |         // TODO(johnlenz): determine if we can limit object literals in some
510 |         // way.
511 |         if (!expr.isObjectLit()) {
512 |           validator.expectCanCast(t, n, castType, exprType);
513 |         }
514 |         ensureTyped(t, n, castType);
515 | 
516 |         if (castType.isSubtype(exprType) || expr.isObjectLit()) {
517 |           expr.setJSType(castType);
518 |         }
519 |         break;
520 | 
521 |       case Token.NAME:
522 |         typeable = visitName(t, n, parent);
523 |         break;
524 | 
525 |       case Token.PARAM_LIST:
526 |         typeable = false;
527 |         break;
528 | 
529 |       case Token.COMMA:
530 |         ensureTyped(t, n, getJSType(n.getLastChild()));
531 |         break;
532 | 
533 |       case Token.TRUE:
534 |       case Token.FALSE:
535 |         ensureTyped(t, n, BOOLEAN_TYPE);
536 |         break;
537 | 
538 |       case Token.THIS:
539 |         ensureTyped(t, n, t.getScope().getTypeOfThis());
540 |         break;
541 | 
542 |       case Token.NULL:
543 |         ensureTyped(t, n, NULL_TYPE);
544 |         break;
545 | 
546 |       case Token.NUMBER:
547 |         ensureTyped(t, n, NUMBER_TYPE);
548 |         break;
549 | 
550 |       case Token.STRING:
551 |         ensureTyped(t, n, STRING_TYPE);
552 |         break;
553 | 
554 |       case Token.STRING_KEY:
555 |         typeable = false;
556 |         break;
557 | 
558 |       case Token.GETTER_DEF:
559 |       case Token.SETTER_DEF:
560 |         // Object literal keys are handled with OBJECTLIT
561 |         break;
562 | 
563 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
564 |         ensureTyped(t, n, ARRAY_TYPE);
565 |         break;
566 | 
567 |       case Token.REGEXP:
568 |         ensureTyped(t, n, REGEXP_TYPE);
569 |         break;
570 | 
571 |       case Token.GETPROP:
572 |         visitGetProp(t, n, parent);
573 |         typeable = !(parent.isAssign() &&
574 |                      parent.getFirstChild() == n);
575 |         break;
576 | 
577 |       case Token.GETELEM:
578 |         visitGetElem(t, n);
579 |         // The type of GETELEM is always unknown, so no point counting that.
580 |         // If that unknown leaks elsewhere (say by an assignment to another
581 |         // variable), then it will be counted.
582 |         typeable = false;
583 |         break;
584 | 
585 |       case Token.VAR:
586 |         visitVar(t, n);
587 |         typeable = false;
588 |         break;
589 | 
590 |       case Token.NEW:
591 |         visitNew(t, n);
592 |         break;
593 | 
594 |       case Token.CALL:
595 |         visitCall(t, n);
596 |         typeable = !parent.isExprResult();
597 |         break;
598 | 
599 |       case Token.RETURN:
600 |         visitReturn(t, n);
601 |         typeable = false;
602 |         break;
603 | 
604 |       case Token.DEC:
605 |       case Token.INC:
606 |         left = n.getFirstChild();
607 |         checkPropCreation(t, left);
608 |         validator.expectNumber(t, left, getJSType(left), "increment/decrement");
609 |         ensureTyped(t, n, NUMBER_TYPE);
610 |         break;
611 | 
612 |       case Token.NOT:
613 |         ensureTyped(t, n, BOOLEAN_TYPE);
614 |         break;
615 | 
616 |       case Token.VOID:
617 |         ensureTyped(t, n, VOID_TYPE);
618 |         break;
619 | 
620 |       case Token.TYPEOF:
621 |         ensureTyped(t, n, STRING_TYPE);
622 |         break;
623 | 
624 |       case Token.BITNOT:
625 |         childType = getJSType(n.getFirstChild());
626 |         if (!childType.matchesInt32Context()) {
627 |           report(t, n, BIT_OPERATION, NodeUtil.opToStr(n.getType()),
628 |               childType.toString());
629 |         }
630 |         ensureTyped(t, n, NUMBER_TYPE);
631 |         break;
632 | 
633 |       case Token.POS:
634 |       case Token.NEG:
635 |         left = n.getFirstChild();
636 |         validator.expectNumber(t, left, getJSType(left), "sign operator");
637 |         ensureTyped(t, n, NUMBER_TYPE);
638 |         break;
639 | 
640 |       case Token.EQ:
641 |       case Token.NE:
642 |       case Token.SHEQ:
643 |       case Token.SHNE: {
644 |         left = n.getFirstChild();
645 |         right = n.getLastChild();
646 | 
647 |         if (left.isTypeOf()) {
648 |           if (right.isString()) {
649 |             checkTypeofString(t, right, right.getString());
650 |           }
651 |         } else if (right.isTypeOf() && left.isString()) {
652 |           checkTypeofString(t, left, left.getString());
653 |         }
654 | 
655 |         leftType = getJSType(left);
656 |         rightType = getJSType(right);
657 | 
658 |         // We do not want to warn about explicit comparisons to VOID. People
659 |         // often do this if they think their type annotations screwed up.
660 |         //
661 |         // We do want to warn about cases where people compare things like
662 |         // (Array|null) == (Function|null)
663 |         // because it probably means they screwed up.
664 |         //
665 |         // This heuristic here is not perfect, but should catch cases we
666 |         // care about without too many false negatives.
667 |         JSType leftTypeRestricted = leftType.restrictByNotNullOrUndefined();
668 |         JSType rightTypeRestricted = rightType.restrictByNotNullOrUndefined();
669 | 
670 |         TernaryValue result = TernaryValue.UNKNOWN;
671 |         if (n.getType() == Token.EQ || n.getType() == Token.NE) {
672 |           result = leftTypeRestricted.testForEquality(rightTypeRestricted);
673 |           if (n.isNE()) {
674 |             result = result.not();
675 |           }
676 |         } else {
677 |           // SHEQ or SHNE
678 |           if (!leftTypeRestricted.canTestForShallowEqualityWith(
679 |                   rightTypeRestricted)) {
680 |             result = n.getType() == Token.SHEQ ?
681 |                 TernaryValue.FALSE : TernaryValue.TRUE;
682 |           }
683 |         }
684 | 
685 |         if (result != TernaryValue.UNKNOWN) {
686 |           report(t, n, DETERMINISTIC_TEST, leftType.toString(),
687 |               rightType.toString(), result.toString());
688 |         }
689 |         ensureTyped(t, n, BOOLEAN_TYPE);
690 |         break;
691 |       }
692 | 
693 |       case Token.LT:
694 |       case Token.LE:
695 |       case Token.GT:
696 |       case Token.GE:
697 |         leftType = getJSType(n.getFirstChild());
698 |         rightType = getJSType(n.getLastChild());
699 |         if (rightType.isNumber()) {
700 |           validator.expectNumber(
701 |               t, n, leftType, "left side of numeric comparison");
702 |         } else if (leftType.isNumber()) {
703 |           validator.expectNumber(
704 |               t, n, rightType, "right side of numeric comparison");
705 |         } else if (leftType.matchesNumberContext() &&
706 |                    rightType.matchesNumberContext()) {
707 |           // OK.
708 |         } else {
709 |           // Whether the comparison is numeric will be determined at runtime
710 |           // each time the expression is evaluated. Regardless, both operands
711 |           // should match a string context.
712 |           String message = "left side of comparison";
713 |           validator.expectString(t, n, leftType, message);
714 |           validator.expectNotNullOrUndefined(
715 |               t, n, leftType, message, getNativeType(STRING_TYPE));
716 |           message = "right side of comparison";
717 |           validator.expectString(t, n, rightType, message);
718 |           validator.expectNotNullOrUndefined(
719 |               t, n, rightType, message, getNativeType(STRING_TYPE));
720 |         }
721 |         ensureTyped(t, n, BOOLEAN_TYPE);
722 |         break;
723 | 
724 |       case Token.IN:
725 |         left = n.getFirstChild();
726 |         right = n.getLastChild();
727 |         rightType = getJSType(right);
728 |         validator.expectString(t, left, getJSType(left), "left side of 'in'");
729 |         validator.expectObject(t, n, rightType, "'in' requires an object");
730 |         if (rightType.isStruct()) {
731 |           report(t, right, IN_USED_WITH_STRUCT);
732 |         }
733 |         ensureTyped(t, n, BOOLEAN_TYPE);
734 |         break;
735 | 
736 |       case Token.INSTANCEOF:
737 |         left = n.getFirstChild();
738 |         right = n.getLastChild();
739 |         rightType = getJSType(right).restrictByNotNullOrUndefined();
740 |         validator.expectAnyObject(
741 |             t, left, getJSType(left), "deterministic instanceof yields false");
742 |         validator.expectActualObject(
743 |             t, right, rightType, "instanceof requires an object");
744 |         ensureTyped(t, n, BOOLEAN_TYPE);
745 |         break;
746 | 
747 |       case Token.ASSIGN:
748 |         visitAssign(t, n);
749 |         typeable = false;
750 |         break;
751 | 
752 |       case Token.ASSIGN_LSH:
753 |       case Token.ASSIGN_RSH:
754 |       case Token.ASSIGN_URSH:
755 |       case Token.ASSIGN_DIV:
756 |       case Token.ASSIGN_MOD:
757 |       case Token.ASSIGN_BITOR:
758 |       case Token.ASSIGN_BITXOR:
759 |       case Token.ASSIGN_BITAND:
760 |       case Token.ASSIGN_SUB:
761 |       case Token.ASSIGN_ADD:
762 |       case Token.ASSIGN_MUL:
763 |         checkPropCreation(t, n.getFirstChild());
764 |         // fall through
765 | 
766 |       case Token.LSH:
767 |       case Token.RSH:
768 |       case Token.URSH:
769 |       case Token.DIV:
770 |       case Token.MOD:
771 |       case Token.BITOR:
772 |       case Token.BITXOR:
773 |       case Token.BITAND:
774 |       case Token.SUB:
775 |       case Token.ADD:
776 |       case Token.MUL:
777 |         visitBinaryOperator(n.getType(), t, n);
778 |         break;
779 | 
780 |       case Token.DELPROP:
781 |         ensureTyped(t, n, BOOLEAN_TYPE);
782 |         break;
783 | 
784 |       case Token.CASE:
785 |         JSType switchType = getJSType(parent.getFirstChild());
786 |         JSType caseType = getJSType(n.getFirstChild());
787 |         validator.expectSwitchMatchesCase(t, n, switchType, caseType);
788 |         typeable = false;
789 |         break;
790 | 
791 |       case Token.WITH: {
792 |         Node child = n.getFirstChild();
793 |         childType = getJSType(child);
794 |         validator.expectObject(t, child, childType, "with requires an object");
795 |         typeable = false;
796 |         break;
797 |       }
798 | 
799 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
800 |         visitFunction(t, n);
801 |         break;
802 | 
803 |       // These nodes have no interesting type behavior.
804 |       case Token.LABEL:
805 |       case Token.LABEL_NAME:
806 |       case Token.SWITCH:
807 |       case Token.BREAK:
808 |       case Token.CATCH:
809 |       case Token.TRY:
810 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
811 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
812 |       case Token.BLOCK:
813 |       case Token.EMPTY:
814 |       case Token.DEFAULT_CASE:
815 |       case Token.CONTINUE:
816 |       case Token.DEBUGGER:
817 |       case Token.THROW:
818 |         typeable = false;
819 |         break;
820 | 
821 |       // These nodes require data flow analysis.
822 |       case Token.DO:
823 |       case Token.IF:
824 |       case Token.WHILE:
825 |         typeable = false;
826 |         break;
827 | 
828 |       case Token.FOR:
829 |         if (NodeUtil.isForIn(n)) {
830 |           Node obj = n.getChildAtIndex(1);
831 |           if (getJSType(obj).isStruct()) {
832 |             report(t, obj, IN_USED_WITH_STRUCT);
833 |           }
834 |         }
835 |         typeable = false;
836 |         break;
837 | 
838 |       // These nodes are typed during the type inference.
839 |       case Token.AND:
840 |       case Token.HOOK:
841 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT:
842 |       case Token.OR:
843 |         if (n.getJSType() != null) { // If we didn't run type inference.
844 |           ensureTyped(t, n);
845 |         } else {
846 |           // If this is an enum, then give that type to the objectlit as well.
847 |           if ((n.isObjectLit())
848 |               && (parent.getJSType() instanceof EnumType)) {
849 |             ensureTyped(t, n, parent.getJSType());
850 |           } else {
851 |             ensureTyped(t, n);
852 |           }
853 |         }
854 |         if (n.isObjectLit()) {
855 |           JSType typ = getJSType(n);
856 |           for (Node key : n.children()) {
857 |             visitObjLitKey(t, key, n, typ);
858 |           }
859 |         }
860 |         break;
861 | 
862 |       default:
863 |         report(t, n, UNEXPECTED_TOKEN, Token.name(n.getType()));
864 |         ensureTyped(t, n);
865 |         break;
866 |     }
867 | 
868 |     // Don't count externs since the user's code may not even use that part.
869 |     typeable = typeable && !inExterns;
870 | 
871 |     if (typeable) {
872 |       doPercentTypedAccounting(t, n);
873 |     }
874 | 
875 |     checkNoTypeCheckSection(n, false);
876 |   }

   *  0 comma ,
   *  1 assignment = += -= *= /= %= <<= >>= >>>= &= ^= |=
   *  2 conditional ?:

   *  4 logical-and &&

   * 10 bitwise shift << >> >>>
   * 11 addition/subtraction + -
   * 12 multiply/divide * / %
   * 13 negation/increment ! ~ - ++ --
   * 14 call, member () [] .

/**
   * Is a FUNCTION node an function expression? An function expression is one
   * that has either no name or a name that is not added to the current scope.
   *
   * <p>Some examples of function expressions:
   * <pre>
   * (function () {})
   * (function f() {})()
   * [ function f() {} ]
   * var f = function f() {};
   * for (function f() {};;) {}
   * </pre>
   *
   * <p>Some examples of functions that are <em>not</em> expressions:
   * <pre>
   * function f() {}
   * if (x); else function f() {}
   * for (;;) { function f() {} }
   * </pre>
   *
   * @param n A node
   * @return Whether n is an function used within an expression.
   */
Method code:
1974 |   static boolean isFunctionExpression(Node n) {
1975 |     return n.isFunction() && !isStatement(n);
1976 |   }

1430 |         if (!input.getProvides().isEmpty() || !input.getRequires().isEmpty()) {
1431 |           continue;
1432 |         }
1433 |       }
1434 | 
1435 |       Node n = input.getAstRoot(this);
1436 | 
1437 |       // Inputs can have a null AST on a parse error.
1438 |       if (n == null) {
1439 |         continue;
1440 |       }
1441 | 
1442 |       JSDocInfo info = n.getJSDocInfo();
1443 |       if (info != null && info.isExterns()) {
1444 |         // If the input file is explicitly marked as an externs file, then
1445 |         // assume the programmer made a mistake and throw it into
1446 |         // the externs pile anyways.
1447 |         externsRoot.addChildToBack(n);
1448 |         input.setIsExtern(true);
1449 | 
1450 |         input.getModule().remove(input);
1451 | 
1452 |         externs.add(input);
1453 |         staleInputs = true;
1454 |       }
1455 |     }
1456 | 
1457 |     if (staleInputs) {
1458 |       repartitionInputs();
1459 |     }
1460 |   }

/**
   * When the CompilerOptions and its WarningsGuard overlap, reconcile
   * any discrepencies.
   */
Method code:
313 |   protected void reconcileOptionsWithGuards() {
314 |     // DiagnosticGroups override the plain checkTypes option.
315 |     if (options.enables(DiagnosticGroups.CHECK_TYPES)) {
316 |       options.checkTypes = true;
317 |     } else if (options.disables(DiagnosticGroups.CHECK_TYPES)) {
318 |       options.checkTypes = false;
319 |     } else if (!options.checkTypes) {
320 |       // If DiagnosticGroups did not override the plain checkTypes
321 |       // option, and checkTypes is enabled, then turn off the
322 |       // parser type warnings.
323 |       options.setWarningLevel(
324 |           DiagnosticGroup.forType(
325 |               RhinoErrorReporter.TYPE_PARSE_ERROR),
326 |           CheckLevel.OFF);
327 |     }
328 | 
329 |     if (options.checkGlobalThisLevel.isOn() &&
330 |         !options.disables(DiagnosticGroups.GLOBAL_THIS)) {
331 |       options.setWarningLevel(
332 |           DiagnosticGroups.GLOBAL_THIS,
333 |           options.checkGlobalThisLevel);
334 |     }
335 | 
336 |     if (options.getLanguageIn() == LanguageMode.ECMASCRIPT5_STRICT) {
337 |       options.setWarningLevel(
338 |           DiagnosticGroups.ES5_STRICT,
339 |           CheckLevel.ERROR);
340 |     }
341 | 
342 |     // All passes must run the variable check. This synthesizes
343 |     // variables later so that the compiler doesn't crash. It also
344 |     // checks the externs file for validity. If you don't want to warn
345 |     // about missing variable declarations, we shut that specific
346 |     // error off.
347 |     if (!options.checkSymbols &&
348 |         !options.enables(DiagnosticGroups.CHECK_VARIABLES)) {
349 |       options.setWarningLevel(
350 |           DiagnosticGroups.CHECK_VARIABLES, CheckLevel.OFF);
351 |     }

   * each object has an implicit prototype, an implicit prototype's

===== M0357 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.FunctionType.supAndInfHelper(FunctionType,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/rhino/jstype/FunctionType.java
Original range: 733-803
Documentation:
/**
   * Computes the supremum or infimum of two functions.
   * Because sup() and inf() share a lot of logic for functions, we use
   * a single helper.
   * @param leastSuper If true, compute the supremum of {@code this} with
   *     {@code that}. Otherwise, compute the infimum.
   * @return The least supertype or greatest subtype.
   */
Method code:
733 |   FunctionType supAndInfHelper(FunctionType that, boolean leastSuper) {
734 |     // NOTE(nicksantos): When we remove the unknown type, the function types
735 |     // form a lattice with the universal constructor at the top of the lattice,
736 |     // and the LEAST_FUNCTION_TYPE type at the bottom of the lattice.
737 |     //
738 |     // When we introduce the unknown type, it's much more difficult to make
739 |     // heads or tails of the partial ordering of types, because there's no
740 |     // clear hierarchy between the different components (parameter types and
741 |     // return types) in the ArrowType.
742 |     //
743 |     // Rather than make the situation more complicated by introducing new
744 |     // types (like unions of functions), we just fallback on the simpler
745 |     // approach of getting things right at the top and the bottom of the
746 |     // lattice.
747 |     //
748 |     // If there are unknown parameters or return types making things
749 |     // ambiguous, then sup(A, B) is always the top function type, and
750 |     // inf(A, B) is always the bottom function type.
751 |     Preconditions.checkNotNull(that);
752 | 
753 |     if (isEquivalentTo(that)) {
754 |       return this;
755 |     }
756 | 
757 |     // If these are ordinary functions, then merge them.
758 |     // Don't do this if any of the params/return
759 |     // values are unknown, because then there will be cycles in
760 |     // their local lattice and they will merge in weird ways.
761 |     if (isOrdinaryFunction() && that.isOrdinaryFunction() &&
762 |         !this.call.hasUnknownParamsOrReturn() &&
763 |         !that.call.hasUnknownParamsOrReturn()) {
764 | 
765 |       // Check for the degenerate case, but double check
766 |       // that there's not a cycle.
767 |       boolean isSubtypeOfThat = isSubtype(that);
768 |       boolean isSubtypeOfThis = that.isSubtype(this);
769 |       if (isSubtypeOfThat && !isSubtypeOfThis) {
770 |         return leastSuper ? that : this;
771 |       } else if (isSubtypeOfThis && !isSubtypeOfThat) {
772 |         return leastSuper ? this : that;
773 |       }
774 | 
775 |       // Merge the two functions component-wise.
776 |       FunctionType merged = tryMergeFunctionPiecewise(that, leastSuper);
777 |       if (merged != null) {
778 |         return merged;
779 |       }
780 |     }
781 | 
782 |     // The function instance type is a special case
783 |     // that lives above the rest of the lattice.
784 |     JSType functionInstance = registry.getNativeType(
785 |         JSTypeNative.FUNCTION_INSTANCE_TYPE);
786 |     if (functionInstance.isEquivalentTo(that)) {
787 |       return leastSuper ? that : this;
788 |     } else if (functionInstance.isEquivalentTo(this)) {
789 |       return leastSuper ? this : that;
790 |     }
791 | 
792 |     // In theory, we should be using the GREATEST_FUNCTION_TYPE as the
793 |     // greatest function. In practice, we don't because it's way too
794 |     // broad. The greatest function takes var_args None parameters, which
795 |     // means that all parameters register a type warning.
796 |     //
797 |     // Instead, we use the U2U ctor type, which has unknown type args.
798 |     FunctionType greatestFn =
799 |         registry.getNativeFunctionType(JSTypeNative.U2U_CONSTRUCTOR_TYPE);
800 |     FunctionType leastFn =
801 |         registry.getNativeFunctionType(JSTypeNative.LEAST_FUNCTION_TYPE);
802 |     return leastSuper ? greatestFn : leastFn;
803 |   }

1327 |         Node n = input.getAstRoot(this);
1328 |         if (hasErrors()) {

1336 |         processAMDAndCommonJSModules();

1346 |           // are not flagged even if they are dropped from the process.
1347 |           for (String provide : input.getProvides()) {
1348 |             getTypeRegistry().forwardDeclareType(provide);
1349 |           }
1350 |         }
1351 | 
1352 |         try {

1355 |               .manageDependencies(options.dependencyOptions, inputs);
1356 |           staleInputs = true;

1369 |         if (hasErrors()) {
1370 |           return null;

===== M0378 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeInference.backwardsInferenceFromCallSite(Node,FunctionType)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/TypeInference.java
Original range: 962-969
Documentation:
/**
   * We only do forward type inference. We do not do full backwards
   * type inference.
   *
   * In other words, if we have,
   * <code>
   * var x = f();
   * g(x);
   * </code>
   * a forward type-inference engine would try to figure out the type
   * of "x" from the return type of "f". A backwards type-inference engine
   * would try to figure out the type of "x" from the parameter type of "g".
   *
   * However, there are a few special syntactic forms where we do some
   * some half-assed backwards type-inference, because programmers
   * expect it in this day and age. To take an example from Java,
   * <code>
   * List<String> x = Lists.newArrayList();
   * </code>
   * The Java compiler will be able to infer the generic type of the List
   * returned by newArrayList().
   *
   * In much the same way, we do some special-case backwards inference for
   * JS. Those cases are enumerated here.
   */
Method code:
962 |   private void backwardsInferenceFromCallSite(Node n, FunctionType fnType) {
963 |     boolean updatedFnType = inferTemplatedTypesForCall(n, fnType);
964 |     if (updatedFnType) {
965 |       fnType = n.getFirstChild().getJSType().toMaybeFunctionType();
966 |     }
967 |     updateTypeOfParameters(n, fnType);
968 |     updateBind(n);
969 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.LinkedFlowScope.FlatFlowScopeCache.FlatFlowScopeCache(LinkedFlowScope,LinkedFlowScope)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/LinkedFlowScope.java
Original range: 423-487
Documentation:
// A cache at the join of two scope chains.
Method code:
423 |     FlatFlowScopeCache(LinkedFlowScope joinedScopeA,
424 |         LinkedFlowScope joinedScopeB) {
425 |       linkedEquivalent = null;
426 | 
427 |       // Always prefer the "real" function scope to the faked-out
428 |       // bottom scope.
429 |       functionScope = joinedScopeA.flowsFromBottom() ?
430 |           joinedScopeB.getFunctionScope() : joinedScopeA.getFunctionScope();
431 | 
432 |       Map<String, StaticSlot<JSType>> slotsA = joinedScopeA.allFlowSlots();
433 |       Map<String, StaticSlot<JSType>> slotsB = joinedScopeB.allFlowSlots();
434 | 
435 |       symbols = slotsA;
436 | 
437 |       // There are 5 different join cases:
438 |       // 1) The type is declared in joinedScopeA, not in joinedScopeB,
439 |       //    and not in functionScope. Just use the one in A.
440 |       // 2) The type is declared in joinedScopeB, not in joinedScopeA,
441 |       //    and not in functionScope. Just use the one in B.
442 |       // 3) The type is declared in functionScope and joinedScopeA, but
443 |       //    not in joinedScopeB. Join the two types.
444 |       // 4) The type is declared in functionScope and joinedScopeB, but
445 |       //    not in joinedScopeA. Join the two types.
446 |       // 5) The type is declared in joinedScopeA and joinedScopeB. Join
447 |       //    the two types.
448 |       Set<String> symbolNames = Sets.newHashSet(symbols.keySet());
449 |       symbolNames.addAll(slotsB.keySet());
450 | 
451 |       for (String name : symbolNames) {
452 |         StaticSlot<JSType> slotA = slotsA.get(name);
453 |         StaticSlot<JSType> slotB = slotsB.get(name);
454 | 
455 |         JSType joinedType = null;
456 |         if (slotB == null || slotB.getType() == null) {
457 |           StaticSlot<JSType> fnSlot
458 |               = joinedScopeB.getFunctionScope().getSlot(name);
459 |           JSType fnSlotType = fnSlot == null ? null : fnSlot.getType();
460 |           if (fnSlotType == null) {
461 |             // Case #1 -- already inserted.
462 |           } else {
463 |             // Case #3
464 |             joinedType = slotA.getType().getLeastSupertype(fnSlotType);
465 |           }
466 |         } else if (slotA == null || slotA.getType() == null) {
467 |           StaticSlot<JSType> fnSlot
468 |               = joinedScopeA.getFunctionScope().getSlot(name);
469 |           JSType fnSlotType = fnSlot == null ? null : fnSlot.getType();
470 |           if (fnSlotType == null) {
471 |             // Case #2
472 |             symbols.put(name, slotB);
473 |           } else {
474 |             // Case #4
475 |             joinedType = slotB.getType().getLeastSupertype(fnSlotType);
476 |           }
477 |         } else {
478 |           // Case #5
479 |           joinedType =
480 |               slotA.getType().getLeastSupertype(slotB.getType());
481 |         }
482 | 
483 |         if (joinedType != null) {
484 |           symbols.put(name, new SimpleSlot(name, joinedType, true));
485 |         }
486 |       }
487 |     }

/**

   *
   * <p>We verify that the enum element type of the enum used
   * for initialization is a subtype of the enum element type of
   * the enum the value is being copied in.</p>
   *
   * <p>Example:</p>
   * <pre>var myEnum = myOtherEnum;</pre>

1985 |       return;

/**
   * Stop the trace.
   * This may only be done once and must be done from the same thread
   * that started it.
   * @param silenceThreshold Traces for time less than silence_threshold
   * ms will be left out of the trace report. A value of -1 indicates
   * that the current ThreadTrace silence_threshold should be used.
   * @return The time that this trace actually ran
   */
Method code:
407 |   long stop(int silenceThreshold) {
408 |     Preconditions.checkState(Thread.currentThread() == startThread);
409 | 
410 |     ThreadTrace trace = getThreadTrace();
411 |     // Do nothing if the thread trace was not initialized.
412 |     if (!trace.isInitialized()) {
413 |       return 0;
414 |     }
415 | 
416 |     stopTimeMs = clock.currentTimeMillis();
417 |     if (extraTracingValues != null) {
418 |       // We use extraTracingValues.length rather than
419 |       // extraTracingStatistics.size() because a new statistic may
420 |       // have been added
421 |       for (int i = 0; i < extraTracingValues.length; i++) {
422 |         long value = extraTracingStatistics.get(i).stop(startThread);
423 |         extraTracingValues[i] = value - extraTracingValues[i];
424 |       }
425 |     }
426 | 
427 |     // Do nothing if the thread trace was not initialized.
428 |     if (!trace.isInitialized()) {
429 |       return 0;
430 |     }
431 | 
432 |     trace.endEvent(this, silenceThreshold);
433 |     return stopTimeMs - startTimeMs;
434 |   }

/**
   * This function takes a set of GETPROP nodes and produces a string that is
   * each property separated by dots. If the node ultimately under the left
   * sub-tree is not a simple name, this is not a valid qualified name.
   *
   * @return a null if this is not a qualified name, or a dot-separated string
   *         of the name and properties.
   */
Method code:
1575 |   public String getQualifiedName() {
1576 |     if (type == Token.NAME) {
1577 |       String name = getString();
1578 |       return name.isEmpty() ? null : name;
1579 |     } else if (type == Token.GETPROP) {
1580 |       String left = getFirstChild().getQualifiedName();
1581 |       if (left == null) {
1582 |         return null;
1583 |       }
1584 |       return left + "." + getLastChild().getString();
1585 |     } else if (type == Token.THIS) {
1586 |       return "this";
1587 |     } else {
1588 |       return null;
1589 |     }
1590 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CodeGenerator.unrollBinaryOperator(Node,int,String,Context,Context,int,int)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CodeGenerator.java
Original range: 772-788
Documentation:
/**
   * We could use addList recursively here, but sometimes we produce
   * very deeply nested operators and run out of stack space, so we
   * just unroll the recursion when possible.
   *
   * We assume nodes are left-recursive.
   */
Method code:
772 |   private void unrollBinaryOperator(
773 |       Node n, int op, String opStr, Context context,
774 |       Context rhsContext, int leftPrecedence, int rightPrecedence) {
775 |     Node firstNonOperator = n.getFirstChild();
776 |     while (firstNonOperator.getType() == op) {
777 |       firstNonOperator = firstNonOperator.getFirstChild();
778 |     }
779 | 
780 |     addExpr(firstNonOperator, leftPrecedence, context);
781 | 
782 |     Node current = firstNonOperator;
783 |     do {
784 |       current = current.getParent();
785 |       cc.addOp(opStr, true);
786 |       addExpr(current.getFirstChild().getNext(), rightPrecedence, rhsContext);
787 |     } while (current != n);
788 |   }

===== M0502 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.parsing.JsDocInfoParser.parseTypeExpression(JsDocToken)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/parsing/JsDocInfoParser.java
Original range: 1825-1868
Documentation:
/**
   * TypeExpression := BasicTypeExpression
   *     | '?' BasicTypeExpression
   *     | '!' BasicTypeExpression
   *     | BasicTypeExpression '?'
   *     | BasicTypeExpression '!'
   *     | '?'
   */
Method code:
1825 |   private Node parseTypeExpression(JsDocToken token) {
1826 |     if (token == JsDocToken.QMARK) {
1827 |       // A QMARK could mean that a type is nullable, or that it's unknown.
1828 |       // We use look-ahead 1 to determine whether it's unknown. Otherwise,
1829 |       // we assume it means nullable. There are 5 cases:
1830 |       // {?} - right curly
1831 |       // {?=} - equals
1832 |       // {function(?, number)} - comma
1833 |       // {function(number, ?)} - right paren
1834 |       // {function(number, ...[?])} - right bracket
1835 |       // {function(): ?|number} - pipe
1836 |       // {Array.<?>} - greater than
1837 |       // I'm not a big fan of using look-ahead for this, but it makes
1838 |       // the type language a lot nicer.
1839 |       token = next();
1840 |       if (token == JsDocToken.COMMA ||
1841 |           token == JsDocToken.EQUALS ||
1842 |           token == JsDocToken.RB ||
1843 |           token == JsDocToken.RC ||
1844 |           token == JsDocToken.RP ||
1845 |           token == JsDocToken.PIPE ||
1846 |           token == JsDocToken.GT) {
1847 |         restoreLookAhead(token);
1848 |         return newNode(Token.QMARK);
1849 |       }
1850 | 
1851 |       return wrapNode(Token.QMARK, parseBasicTypeExpression(token));
1852 |     } else if (token == JsDocToken.BANG) {
1853 |       return wrapNode(Token.BANG, parseBasicTypeExpression(next()));
1854 |     } else {
1855 |       Node basicTypeExpr = parseBasicTypeExpression(token);
1856 |       if (basicTypeExpr != null) {
1857 |         if (match(JsDocToken.QMARK)) {
1858 |           next();
1859 |           return wrapNode(Token.QMARK, basicTypeExpr);
1860 |         } else if (match(JsDocToken.BANG)) {
1861 |           next();
1862 |           return wrapNode(Token.BANG, basicTypeExpr);
1863 |         }
1864 |       }
1865 | 
1866 |       return basicTypeExpr;
1867 |     }
1868 |   }

===== M0503 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.JSType.isSubtype(JSType)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/rhino/jstype/JSType.java
Original range: 1228-1230
Documentation:
/**
   * Checks whether {@code this} is a subtype of {@code that}.<p>
   *
   * Subtyping rules:
   * <ul>
   * <li>(unknown) &mdash; every type is a subtype of the Unknown type.</li>
   * <li>(no) &mdash; the No type is a subtype of every type.</li>
   * <li>(no-object) &mdash; the NoObject type is a subtype of every object
   * type (i.e. subtypes of the Object type).</li>
   * <li>(ref) &mdash; a type is a subtype of itself.</li>
   * <li>(union-l) &mdash; A union type is a subtype of a type U if all the
   * union type's constituents are a subtype of U. Formally<br>
   * {@code (T<sub>1</sub>, &hellip;, T<sub>n</sub>) &lt;: U} if and only
   * {@code T<sub>k</sub> &lt;: U} for all {@code k &isin; 1..n}.</li>
   * <li>(union-r) &mdash; A type U is a subtype of a union type if it is a
   * subtype of one of the union type's constituents. Formally<br>
   * {@code U &lt;: (T<sub>1</sub>, &hellip;, T<sub>n</sub>)} if and only
   * if {@code U &lt;: T<sub>k</sub>} for some index {@code k}.</li>
   * <li>(objects) &mdash; an Object {@code O<sub>1</sub>} is a subtype
   * of an object {@code O<sub>2</sub>} if it has more properties
   * than {@code O<sub>2</sub>} and all common properties are
   * pairwise subtypes.</li>
   * </ul>
   *
   * @return {@code this &lt;: that}
   */
Method code:
1228 |   public boolean isSubtype(JSType that) {
1229 |     return isSubtypeHelper(this, that);
1230 |   }

===== M0522 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.DataFlowAnalysis.analyze(int)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/DataFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 201-229
Documentation:
/**
   * Finds a fixed-point solution. The function has the side effect of replacing
   * the existing node annotations with the computed solutions using {@link
   * com.google.javascript.jscomp.graph.GraphNode#setAnnotation(Annotation)}.
   *
   * <p>Initially, each node's input and output flow state contains the value
   * given by {@link #createInitialEstimateLattice()} (with the exception of the
   * entry node of the graph which takes on the {@link #createEntryLattice()}
   * value. Each node will use the output state of its predecessor and compute a
   * output state according to the instruction. At that time, any nodes that
   * depends on the node's newly modified output value will need to recompute
   * their output state again. Each step will perform a computation at one node
   * until no extra computation will modify any existing output state anymore.
   *
   * @param maxSteps Max number of iterations before the method stops and throw
   *        a {@link MaxIterationsExceededException}. This will prevent the
   *        analysis from going into a infinite loop.
   */
Method code:
201 |   final void analyze(int maxSteps) {
202 |     initialize();
203 |     int step = 0;
204 |     while (!orderedWorkSet.isEmpty()) {
205 |       if (step > maxSteps) {
206 |         throw new MaxIterationsExceededException(
207 |           "Analysis did not terminate after " + maxSteps + " iterations");
208 |       }
209 |       DiGraphNode<N, Branch> curNode = orderedWorkSet.iterator().next();
210 |       orderedWorkSet.remove(curNode);
211 |       joinInputs(curNode);
212 |       if (flow(curNode)) {
213 |         // If there is a change in the current node, we want to grab the list
214 |         // of nodes that this node affects.
215 |         List<DiGraphNode<N, Branch>> nextNodes = isForward() ?
216 |             cfg.getDirectedSuccNodes(curNode) :
217 |             cfg.getDirectedPredNodes(curNode);
218 |         for (DiGraphNode<N, Branch> nextNode : nextNodes) {
219 |           if (nextNode != cfg.getImplicitReturn()) {
220 |             orderedWorkSet.add(nextNode);
221 |           }
222 |         }
223 |       }
224 |       step++;
225 |     }
226 |     if (isForward()) {
227 |       joinInputs(getCfg().getImplicitReturn());
228 |     }
229 |   }
