/**
   * Infer the parameter and return types of a function from
   * the parameter and return types of the function it is overriding.
   *
   * @param oldType The function being overridden. Does nothing if this is null.
   * @param paramsParent The LP node of the function that we're assigning to.
   *     If null, that just means we're not initializing this to a function
   *     literal.
   */
Method code:
249 |   FunctionTypeBuilder inferFromOverriddenFunction(
250 |       @Nullable FunctionType oldType, @Nullable Node paramsParent) {
251 |     if (oldType == null) {
252 |       return this;
253 |     }
254 | 
255 |     returnType = oldType.getReturnType();
256 |     returnTypeInferred = oldType.isReturnTypeInferred();
257 |     if (paramsParent == null) {
258 |       // Not a function literal.
259 |       parametersNode = oldType.getParametersNode();
260 |       if (parametersNode == null) {
261 |         parametersNode = new FunctionParamBuilder(typeRegistry).build();
262 |       }
263 |     } else {
264 |       // We're overriding with a function literal. Apply type information
265 |       // to each parameter of the literal.
266 |       FunctionParamBuilder paramBuilder =
267 |           new FunctionParamBuilder(typeRegistry);
268 |       Iterator<Node> oldParams = oldType.getParameters().iterator();
269 |       boolean warnedAboutArgList = false;
270 |       boolean oldParamsListHitOptArgs = false;
271 |       for (Node currentParam = paramsParent.getFirstChild();
272 |            currentParam != null; currentParam = currentParam.getNext()) {
273 |         if (oldParams.hasNext()) {
274 |           Node oldParam = oldParams.next();
275 |           Node newParam = paramBuilder.newParameterFromNode(oldParam);
276 | 
277 |           oldParamsListHitOptArgs = oldParamsListHitOptArgs ||
278 |               oldParam.isVarArgs() ||
279 |               oldParam.isOptionalArg();
280 | 
281 |           // The subclass method might write its var_args as individual
282 |           // arguments.
283 |           if (currentParam.getNext() != null && newParam.isVarArgs()) {
284 |             newParam.setVarArgs(false);
285 |             newParam.setOptionalArg(true);
286 |           }
287 |         } else {
288 |           warnedAboutArgList |= addParameter(
289 |               paramBuilder,
290 |               typeRegistry.getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE),
291 |               warnedAboutArgList,
292 |               codingConvention.isOptionalParameter(currentParam) ||
293 |                   oldParamsListHitOptArgs,
294 |               codingConvention.isVarArgsParameter(currentParam));
295 |         }
296 |       }
297 | 
298 |       // Clone any remaining params that aren't in the function literal,
299 |       // but make them optional.
300 |       while (oldParams.hasNext()) {
301 |         paramBuilder.newOptionalParameterFromNode(oldParams.next());
302 |       }
303 | 
304 |       parametersNode = paramBuilder.build();
305 |     }
306 |     return this;
307 |   }

/**
     * Move all the functions that are valid at the execution of the first
     * statement of the function to the beginning of the function definition.
     */
Method code:
647 |     private void moveNamedFunctions(Node functionBody) {
648 |       Preconditions.checkState(
649 |           functionBody.getParent().isFunction());
650 |       Node previous = null;
651 |       Node current = functionBody.getFirstChild();
652 |       // Skip any declarations at the beginning of the function body, they
653 |       // are already in the right place.

655 |         previous = current;
656 |         current = current.getNext();

673 |         } else {
674 |           // Update the previous only if the current node hasn't been moved.
675 |           previous = current;
676 |         }

678 |       }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.handleStmtList(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 484-523

Method code:
484 |   private void handleStmtList(Node node) {
485 |     Node parent = node.getParent();
486 |     // Special case, don't add a block of empty CATCH block to the graph.
487 |     if (node.isBlock() && parent != null &&
488 |         parent.isTry() &&
489 |         NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(parent) == node &&
490 |         !NodeUtil.hasCatchHandler(node)) {
491 |       return;

495 |     Node child = node.getFirstChild();

497 |     // Function declarations are skipped since control doesn't go into that

501 |     }

505 |     } else {

507 |     }

513 |         case Token.CASE:
514 |         case Token.TRY:

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.Normalize.NormalizeStatements.extractForInitializer(Node,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/Normalize.java
Original range: 567-614
Documentation:
/**
     * Bring the initializers out of FOR loops.  These need to be placed
     * before any associated LABEL nodes. This needs to be done from the top
     * level label first so this is called as a pre-order callback (from
     * shouldTraverse).
     *
     * @param n The node to inspect.
     * @param before The node to insert the initializer before.
     * @param beforeParent The parent of the node before which the initializer
     *     will be inserted.
     */
Method code:
567 |     private void extractForInitializer(
568 |         Node n, Node before, Node beforeParent) {
569 | 
570 |       for (Node next, c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = next) {
571 |         next = c.getNext();
572 |         Node insertBefore = (before == null) ? c : before;
573 |         Node insertBeforeParent = (before == null) ? n : beforeParent;
574 |         switch (c.getType()) {
575 |           case Token.LABEL:
576 |             extractForInitializer(c, insertBefore, insertBeforeParent);
577 |             break;
578 |           case Token.FOR:
579 |             if (NodeUtil.isForIn(c)) {
580 |               Node first = c.getFirstChild();
581 |               if (first.isVar()) {
582 |                 // Transform:
583 |                 //    for (var a = 1 in b) {}
584 |                 // to:
585 |                 //    var a = 1; for (a in b) {};
586 |                 Node newStatement = first;
587 |                 // Clone just the node, to remove any initialization.
588 |                 Node name = newStatement.getFirstChild().cloneNode();
589 |                 first.getParent().replaceChild(first, name);
590 |                 insertBeforeParent.addChildBefore(newStatement, insertBefore);
591 |                 reportCodeChange("FOR-IN var declaration");
592 |               }
593 |             } else if (!c.getFirstChild().isEmpty()) {
594 |               Node init = c.getFirstChild();
595 |               Node empty = IR.empty();
596 |               empty.copyInformationFrom(c);
597 |               c.replaceChild(init, empty);
598 | 
599 |               Node newStatement;
600 |               // Only VAR statements, and expressions are allowed,
601 |               // but are handled differently.
602 |               if (init.isVar()) {
603 |                 newStatement = init;
604 |               } else {
605 |                 newStatement = NodeUtil.newExpr(init);
606 |               }
607 | 
608 |               insertBeforeParent.addChildBefore(newStatement, insertBefore);
609 |               reportCodeChange("FOR initializer");
610 |             }
611 |             break;
612 |         }
613 |       }
614 |     }

/**
   * Emit a warning if we can prove that a property cannot possibly be
   * defined on an object. Note the difference between JS and a strictly
   * statically typed language: we're checking if the property
   * *cannot be defined*, whereas a java compiler would check if the
   * property *can be undefined*.
   */
Method code:
1429 |   private void checkPropertyAccess(JSType childType, String propName,
1430 |       NodeTraversal t, Node n) {
1431 |     // If the property type is unknown, check the object type to see if it
1432 |     // can ever be defined. We explicitly exclude CHECKED_UNKNOWN (for
1433 |     // properties where we've checked that it exists, or for properties on
1434 |     // objects that aren't in this binary).
1435 |     JSType propType = getJSType(n);
1436 |     if (propType.isEquivalentTo(typeRegistry.getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE))) {
1437 |       childType = childType.autobox();
1438 |       ObjectType objectType = ObjectType.cast(childType);
1439 |       if (objectType != null) {
1440 |         // We special-case object types so that checks on enums can be
1441 |         // much stricter, and so that we can use hasProperty (which is much
1442 |         // faster in most cases).
1443 |         if (!objectType.hasProperty(propName) ||
1444 |             objectType.isEquivalentTo(
1445 |                 typeRegistry.getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE))) {
1446 |           if (objectType instanceof EnumType) {
1447 |             report(t, n, INEXISTENT_ENUM_ELEMENT, propName);
1448 |           } else {
1449 |             checkPropertyAccessHelper(objectType, propName, t, n);
1450 |           }
1451 |         }
1452 | 
1453 |       } else {
1454 |         checkPropertyAccessHelper(childType, propName, t, n);
1455 |       }
1456 |     }
1457 |   }

/**
   * Returns a constructor function either by returning it from the
   * registry if it exists or creating and registering a new type. If
   * there is already a type, then warn if the existing type is
   * different than the one we are creating, though still return the
   * existing function if possible.  The primary purpose of this is
   * that registering a constructor will fail for all built-in types
   * that are initialized in {@link JSTypeRegistry}.  We a) want to
   * make sure that the type information specified in the externs file
   * matches what is in the registry and b) annotate the externs with
   * the {@link JSType} from the registry so that there are not two
   * separate JSType objects for one type.
   */
Method code:

740 |     JSType existingType = typeRegistry.getType(fnName);
741 | 
742 |     if (makesStructs) {
743 |       fnType.setStruct();
744 |     } else if (makesDicts) {
745 |       fnType.setDict();
746 |     }
747 |     if (existingType != null) {
748 |       boolean isInstanceObject = existingType.isInstanceType();
749 |       if (isInstanceObject || fnName.equals("Function")) {
750 |         FunctionType existingFn =
751 |             isInstanceObject ?
752 |             existingType.toObjectType().getConstructor() :
753 |             typeRegistry.getNativeFunctionType(FUNCTION_FUNCTION_TYPE);
754 | 
755 |         if (existingFn.getSource() == null) {
756 |           existingFn.setSource(contents.getSourceNode());
757 |         }
758 |

760 |           reportWarning(TYPE_REDEFINITION, formatFnName(),
761 |               fnType.toString(), existingFn.toString());
762 |         }
763 | 
764 |         return existingFn;
765 |       } else {
766 |         // We fall through and return the created type, even though it will fail
767 |         // to register. We have no choice as we have to return a function. We
768 |         // issue an error elsewhere though, so the user should fix it.
769 |       }
770 |     }

772 |     maybeSetBaseType(fnType);
773 | 
774 |     if (getScopeDeclaredIn().isGlobal() && !fnName.isEmpty()) {
775 |       typeRegistry.declareType(fnName, fnType.getInstanceType());
776 |     }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypedScopeCreator.AbstractScopeBuilder.isQualifiedNameInferred(String,Node,JSDocInfo,Node,JSType)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/TypedScopeCreator.java
Original range: 1661-1715
Documentation:
/**
     * Determines whether a qualified name is inferred.
     * NOTE(nicksantos): Determining whether a property is declared or not
     * is really really obnoxious.
     *
     * The problem is that there are two (equally valid) coding styles:
     *
     * (function() {
     *   /* The authoritative definition of goog.bar. /
     *   goog.bar = function() {};
     * })();
     *
     * function f() {
     *   goog.bar();
     *   /* Reset goog.bar to a no-op. /
     *   goog.bar = function() {};
     * }
     *
     * In a dynamic language with first-class functions, it's very difficult
     * to know which one the user intended without looking at lots of
     * contextual information (the second example demonstrates a small case
     * of this, but there are some really pathological cases as well).
     *
     * The current algorithm checks if either the declaration has
     * JsDoc type information, or @const with a known type,
     * or a function literal with a name we haven't seen before.
     */
Method code:
1661 |     private boolean isQualifiedNameInferred(
1662 |         String qName, Node n, JSDocInfo info,
1663 |         Node rhsValue, JSType valueType) {
1664 |       if (valueType == null) {
1665 |         return true;
1666 |       }
1667 | 
1668 |       // Prototypes of constructors and interfaces are always declared.
1669 |       if (qName != null && qName.endsWith(".prototype")) {
1670 |         String className = qName.substring(0, qName.lastIndexOf(".prototype"));
1671 |         Var slot = scope.getSlot(className);
1672 |         JSType classType = slot == null ? null : slot.getType();
1673 |         if (classType != null
1674 |             && (classType.isConstructor() || classType.isInterface())) {
1675 |           return false;
1676 |         }
1677 |       }
1678 | 
1679 |       boolean inferred = true;
1680 |       if (info != null) {
1681 |         inferred = !(info.hasType()
1682 |             || info.hasEnumParameterType()
1683 |             || (isConstantSymbol(info, n) && valueType != null
1684 |                 && !valueType.isUnknownType())
1685 |             || FunctionTypeBuilder.isFunctionTypeDeclaration(info));
1686 |       }
1687 | 
1688 |       if (inferred && rhsValue != null && rhsValue.isFunction()) {
1689 |         if (info != null) {
1690 |           return false;
1691 |         } else if (!scope.isDeclared(qName, false) &&
1692 |             n.isUnscopedQualifiedName()) {
1693 | 
1694 |           // Check if this is in a conditional block.
1695 |           // Functions assigned in conditional blocks are inferred.
1696 |           for (Node current = n.getParent();
1697 |                !(current.isScript() || current.isFunction());
1698 |                current = current.getParent()) {
1699 |             if (NodeUtil.isControlStructure(current)) {
1700 |               return true;
1701 |             }
1702 |           }
1703 | 
1704 |           // Check if this is assigned in an inner scope.
1705 |           // Functions assigned in inner scopes are inferred.
1706 |           AstFunctionContents contents =
1707 |               getFunctionAnalysisResults(scope.getRootNode());
1708 |           if (contents == null ||
1709 |               !contents.getEscapedQualifiedNames().contains(qName)) {
1710 |             return false;
1711 |           }
1712 |         }
1713 |       }
1714 |       return inferred;
1715 |     }

/**
     * Processes a property, adding it to the list of properties to rename.
     * @return a representative type for the property reference, which will be
     *   the highest type on the prototype chain of the provided type.  In the
     *   case of a union type, it will be the highest type on the prototype
     *   chain of one of the members of the union.
     */
Method code:
544 |     private T processProperty(
545 |         NodeTraversal t, Property prop, T type, T relatedType) {
546 |       type = typeSystem.restrictByNotNullOrUndefined(type);
547 |       if (prop.skipRenaming || typeSystem.isInvalidatingType(type)) {
548 |         return null;
549 |       }
550 | 
551 |       Iterable<T> alternatives = typeSystem.getTypeAlternatives(type);
552 |       if (alternatives != null) {
553 |         T firstType = relatedType;
554 |         for (T subType : alternatives) {
555 |           T lastType = processProperty(t, prop, subType, firstType);
556 |           if (lastType != null) {
557 |             firstType = firstType == null ? lastType : firstType;
558 |           }
559 |         }
560 |         return firstType;
561 |       } else {
562 |         T topType = typeSystem.getTypeWithProperty(prop.name, type);
563 |         if (typeSystem.isInvalidatingType(topType)) {
564 |           return null;
565 |         }
566 |         prop.addType(type, topType, relatedType);
567 |         return topType;
568 |       }
569 |     }

   * character set - that they have UTF-16 values equal to or below 0x7f.
   * This check can find which identifiers with Unicode characters need to be
   * escaped in order to allow resulting files to be processed by non-Unicode

239 |   void addNumber(double x) {
240 |     // This is not pretty printing. This is to prevent misparsing of x- -4 as
241 |     // x--4 (which is a syntax error).
242 |     char prev = getLastChar();
243 |     boolean negativeZero = isNegativeZero(x);
244 |     if ((x < 0 || negativeZero) && prev == '-') {
245 |       add(" ");
246 |     }
247 |

255 |         while (mantissa / 10 * Math.pow(10, exp + 1) == value) {
256 |           mantissa /= 10;
257 |           exp++;
258 |         }
259 |       }
260 |       if (exp > 2) {
261 |         addConstant(Long.toString(mantissa) + "E" + Integer.toString(exp));
262 |       } else {

264 |         if (Long.toHexString(valueAbs).length() + 2 <
265 |             Long.toString(valueAbs).length()) {

267 |               Long.toHexString(valueAbs));
268 |         } else {
269 |           addConstant(Long.toString(value));

271 |       }
272 |     } else {

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeInference.ensurePropertyDefined(Node,JSType)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/TypeInference.java
Original range: 567-635
Documentation:
/**
   * Defines a property if the property has not been defined yet.
   */
Method code:
567 |   private void ensurePropertyDefined(Node getprop, JSType rightType) {
568 |     String propName = getprop.getLastChild().getString();
569 |     Node obj = getprop.getFirstChild();
570 |     JSType nodeType = getJSType(obj);
571 |     ObjectType objectType = ObjectType.cast(
572 |         nodeType.restrictByNotNullOrUndefined());
573 |     boolean propCreationInConstructor = obj.isThis() &&
574 |         getJSType(syntacticScope.getRootNode()).isConstructor();
575 | 
576 |     if (objectType == null) {
577 |       registry.registerPropertyOnType(propName, nodeType);
578 |     } else {
579 |       if (nodeType.isStruct() && !objectType.hasProperty(propName)) {
580 |         // In general, we don't want to define a property on a struct object,
581 |         // b/c TypeCheck will later check for improper property creation on
582 |         // structs. There are two exceptions.
583 |         // 1) If it's a property created inside the constructor, on the newly
584 |         //    created instance, allow it.
585 |         // 2) If it's a prototype property, allow it. For example:
586 |         //    Foo.prototype.bar = baz;
587 |         //    where Foo.prototype is a struct and the assignment happens at the
588 |         //    top level and the constructor Foo is defined in the same file.
589 |         boolean staticPropCreation = false;
590 |         Node maybeAssignStm = getprop.getParent().getParent();
591 |         if (syntacticScope.isGlobal() &&
592 |             NodeUtil.isPrototypePropertyDeclaration(maybeAssignStm)) {
593 |           String propCreationFilename = maybeAssignStm.getSourceFileName();
594 |           Node ctor = objectType.getOwnerFunction().getSource();
595 |           if (ctor != null &&
596 |               ctor.getSourceFileName().equals(propCreationFilename)) {
597 |             staticPropCreation = true;
598 |           }
599 |         }
600 |         if (!propCreationInConstructor && !staticPropCreation) {
601 |           return; // Early return to avoid creating the property below.
602 |         }
603 |       }
604 | 
605 |       if (ensurePropertyDeclaredHelper(getprop, objectType)) {
606 |         return;
607 |       }
608 | 
609 |       if (!objectType.isPropertyTypeDeclared(propName)) {
610 |         // We do not want a "stray" assign to define an inferred property
611 |         // for every object of this type in the program. So we use a heuristic
612 |         // approach to determine whether to infer the property.
613 |         //
614 |         // 1) If the property is already defined, join it with the previously
615 |         //    inferred type.
616 |         // 2) If this isn't an instance object, define it.
617 |         // 3) If the property of an object is being assigned in the constructor,
618 |         //    define it.
619 |         // 4) If this is a stub, define it.
620 |         // 5) Otherwise, do not define the type, but declare it in the registry
621 |         //    so that we can use it for missing property checks.
622 |         if (objectType.hasProperty(propName) || !objectType.isInstanceType()) {
623 |           if ("prototype".equals(propName)) {
624 |             objectType.defineDeclaredProperty(propName, rightType, getprop);
625 |           } else {
626 |             objectType.defineInferredProperty(propName, rightType, getprop);
627 |           }
628 |         } else if (propCreationInConstructor) {
629 |           objectType.defineInferredProperty(propName, rightType, getprop);
630 |         } else {
631 |           registry.registerPropertyOnType(propName, objectType);
632 |         }
633 |       }
634 |     }
635 |   }

Method code:
677 |   private FlowScope traverseName(Node n, FlowScope scope) {
678 |     String varName = n.getString();
679 |     Node value = n.getFirstChild();
680 |     JSType type = n.getJSType();
681 |     if (value != null) {
682 |       scope = traverse(value, scope);
683 |       updateScopeForTypeChange(scope, n, n.getJSType() /* could be null */,
684 |           getJSType(value));
685 |       return scope;
686 |     } else {
687 |       StaticSlot<JSType> var = scope.getSlot(varName);
688 |       if (var != null) {
689 |         // There are two situations where we don't want to use type information
690 |         // from the scope, even if we have it.
691 | 
692 |         // 1) The var is escaped and assigned in an inner scope, e.g.,
693 |         // function f() { var x = 3; function g() { x = null } (x); }
694 |         boolean isInferred = var.isTypeInferred();
695 |         boolean unflowable = isInferred &&
696 |             isUnflowable(syntacticScope.getVar(varName));
697 | 
698 |         // 2) We're reading type information from another scope for an
699 |         // inferred variable. That variable is assigned more than once,
700 |         // and we can't know which type we're getting.
701 |         //
702 |         // var t = null; function f() { (t); } doStuff(); t = {};
703 |         //
704 |         // Notice that this heuristic isn't perfect. For example, you might
705 |         // have:
706 |         //
707 |         // function f() { (t); } f(); var t = 3;
708 |         //
709 |         // In this case, we would infer the first reference to t as
710 |         // type {number}, even though it's undefined.
711 |         boolean nonLocalInferredSlot = false;
712 |         if (isInferred && syntacticScope.isLocal()) {
713 |           Var maybeOuterVar = syntacticScope.getParent().getVar(varName);
714 |           if (var == maybeOuterVar &&
715 |               !maybeOuterVar.isMarkedAssignedExactlyOnce()) {
716 |             nonLocalInferredSlot = true;
717 |           }
718 |         }
719 | 
720 |         if (!unflowable && !nonLocalInferredSlot) {
721 |           type = var.getType();
722 |           if (type == null) {
723 |             type = unknownType;
724 |           }
725 |         }
726 |       }
727 |     }
728 |     n.setJSType(type);
729 |     return scope;
730 |   }

/**
   * Enforces type casts, and ensures the node is typed.
   *
   * A cast in the way that we use it in JSDoc annotations never
   * alters the generated code and therefore never can induce any runtime
   * operation. What this means is that a 'cast' is really just a compile
   * time constraint on the underlying value. In the future, we may add
   * support for run-time casts for compiled tests.
   *
   * To ensure some shred of sanity, we enforce the notion that the
   * type you are casting to may only meaningfully be a narrower type
   * than the underlying declared type. We also invalidate optimizations
   * on bad type casts.
   *
   * @param t The traversal object needed to report errors.
   * @param n The node getting a type assigned to it.
   * @param type The type to be assigned.
   */
Method code:
2054 |   private void ensureTyped(NodeTraversal t, Node n, JSType type) {
2055 |     // Make sure FUNCTION nodes always get function type.
2056 |     Preconditions.checkState(!n.isFunction() ||
2057 |             type.isFunctionType() ||
2058 |             type.isUnknownType());
2059 |     // TODO(johnlenz): this seems like a strange place to check "@implicitCast"
2060 |     JSDocInfo info = n.getJSDocInfo();
2061 |     if (info != null) {
2062 |       if (info.isImplicitCast() && !inExterns) {
2063 |         String propName = n.isGetProp() ?
2064 |             n.getLastChild().getString() : "(missing)";
2065 |         compiler.report(
2066 |             t.makeError(n, ILLEGAL_IMPLICIT_CAST, propName));
2067 |       }
2068 |     }
2069 | 
2070 |     if (n.getJSType() == null) {
2071 |       n.setJSType(type);
2072 |     }
2073 |   }

/**
   * Merges the line number and character number in one integer. The Character
   * number takes the first 12 bits and the line number takes the rest. If
   * the character number is greater than <code>2<sup>12</sup>-1</code> it is
   * adjusted to <code>2<sup>12</sup>-1</code>.
   */
Method code:
1193 |   protected static int mergeLineCharNo(int lineno, int charno) {
1194 |     if (lineno < 0 || charno < 0) {

1197 |       return lineno << COLUMN_BITS | COLUMN_MASK;
1198 |     } else {

1200 |     }
1201 |   }

===== M0815 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CodeGenerator.strEscape(String,char,String,String,String,CharsetEncoder,boolean,boolean)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CodeGenerator.java
Original range: 1051-1174
Documentation:
/** Helper to escape JavaScript string as well as regular expression */
Method code:
1051 |   private String strEscape(
1052 |       String s,
1053 |       char quote,
1054 |       String doublequoteEscape,
1055 |       String singlequoteEscape,
1056 |       String backslashEscape,
1057 |       CharsetEncoder outputCharsetEncoder,
1058 |       boolean useSlashV,
1059 |       boolean isRegexp) {
1060 |     StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder(s.length() + 2);
1061 |     sb.append(quote);
1062 |     for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {
1063 |       char c = s.charAt(i);
1064 |       switch (c) {
1065 |         case '\0': sb.append("\\x00"); break;
1066 |         case '\u000B':
1067 |           if (useSlashV) {
1068 |             sb.append("\\v");
1069 |           } else {
1070 |             sb.append("\\x0B");
1071 |           }
1072 |           break;
1073 |         // From the SingleEscapeCharacter grammar production.
1074 |         case '\b': sb.append("\\b"); break;
1075 |         case '\f': sb.append("\\f"); break;
1076 |         case '\n': sb.append("\\n"); break;
1077 |         case '\r': sb.append("\\r"); break;
1078 |         case '\t': sb.append("\\t"); break;
1079 |         case '\\': sb.append(backslashEscape); break;
1080 |         case '\"': sb.append(doublequoteEscape); break;
1081 |         case '\'': sb.append(singlequoteEscape); break;
1082 | 
1083 |         // From LineTerminators (ES5 Section 7.3, Table 3)
1084 |         case '\u2028': sb.append("\\u2028"); break;
1085 |         case '\u2029': sb.append("\\u2029"); break;
1086 | 
1087 |         case '=':
1088 |           // '=' is a syntactically signficant regexp character.
1089 |           if (trustedStrings || isRegexp) {
1090 |             sb.append(c);
1091 |           } else {
1092 |             sb.append("\\x3d");
1093 |           }
1094 |           break;
1095 | 
1096 |         case '&':
1097 |           if (trustedStrings || isRegexp) {
1098 |             sb.append(c);
1099 |           } else {
1100 |             sb.append("\\x26");
1101 |           }
1102 |           break;
1103 | 
1104 |         case '>':
1105 |           if (!trustedStrings && !isRegexp) {
1106 |             sb.append(GT_ESCAPED);
1107 |             break;
1108 |           }
1109 | 
1110 |           // Break --> into --\> or ]]> into ]]\>
1111 |           //
1112 |           // This is just to prevent developers from shooting themselves in the
1113 |           // foot, and does not provide the level of security that you get
1114 |           // with trustedString == false.
1115 |           if (i >= 2 &&
1116 |               ((s.charAt(i - 1) == '-' && s.charAt(i - 2) == '-') ||
1117 |                (s.charAt(i - 1) == ']' && s.charAt(i - 2) == ']'))) {
1118 |             sb.append(GT_ESCAPED);
1119 |           } else {
1120 |             sb.append(c);
1121 |           }
1122 |           break;
1123 |         case '<':
1124 |           if (!trustedStrings && !isRegexp) {
1125 |             sb.append(LT_ESCAPED);
1126 |             break;
1127 |           }
1128 | 
1129 |           // Break </script into <\/script
1130 |           // As above, this is just to prevent developers from doing this
1131 |           // accidentally.
1132 |           final String endScript = "/script";
1133 | 
1134 |           // Break <!-- into <\!--
1135 |           final String startComment = "!--";
1136 | 
1137 |           if (s.regionMatches(true, i + 1, endScript, 0,
1138 |                               endScript.length())) {
1139 |             sb.append(LT_ESCAPED);
1140 |           } else if (s.regionMatches(false, i + 1, startComment, 0,
1141 |                                      startComment.length())) {
1142 |             sb.append(LT_ESCAPED);
1143 |           } else {
1144 |             sb.append(c);
1145 |           }
1146 |           break;
1147 |         default:
1148 |           // If we're given an outputCharsetEncoder, then check if the
1149 |           //  character can be represented in this character set.
1150 |           if (outputCharsetEncoder != null) {
1151 |             if (outputCharsetEncoder.canEncode(c)) {
1152 |               sb.append(c);
1153 |             } else {
1154 |               // Unicode-escape the character.
1155 |               appendHexJavaScriptRepresentation(sb, c);
1156 |             }
1157 |           } else {
1158 |             // No charsetEncoder provided - pass straight Latin characters
1159 |             // through, and escape the rest.  Doing the explicit character
1160 |             // check is measurably faster than using the CharsetEncoder.
1161 |             if (c > 0x1f && c < 0x7f) {
1162 |               sb.append(c);
1163 |             } else {
1164 |               // Other characters can be misinterpreted by some JS parsers,
1165 |               // or perhaps mangled by proxies along the way,
1166 |               // so we play it safe and Unicode escape them.
1167 |               appendHexJavaScriptRepresentation(sb, c);
1168 |             }
1169 |           }
1170 |       }
1171 |     }
1172 |     sb.append(quote);
1173 |     return sb.toString();
1174 |   }

===== M0817 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.DisambiguateProperties.Property.expandTypesToSkip()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/DisambiguateProperties.java
Original range: 194-231
Documentation:
/** Invalidates any types related to invalid types. */
Method code:
194 |     void expandTypesToSkip() {
195 |       // If we are not going to rename any properties, then we do not need to
196 |       // update the list of invalid types, as they are all invalid.
197 |       if (shouldRename()) {
198 |         int count = 0;
199 |         while (true) {
200 |           // It should usually only take one time through this do-while.
201 |           checkState(++count < 10, "Stuck in loop expanding types to skip.");
202 | 
203 |           // Make sure that the representative type for each type to skip is
204 |           // marked as being skipped.
205 |           Set<T> rootTypesToSkip = Sets.newHashSet();
206 |           for (T subType : typesToSkip) {
207 |             rootTypesToSkip.add(types.find(subType));
208 |           }
209 |           typesToSkip.addAll(rootTypesToSkip);
210 | 
211 |           Set<T> newTypesToSkip = Sets.newHashSet();
212 |           Set<T> allTypes = types.elements();
213 |           int originalTypesSize = allTypes.size();
214 |           for (T subType : allTypes) {
215 |             if (!typesToSkip.contains(subType)
216 |                 && typesToSkip.contains(types.find(subType))) {
217 |               newTypesToSkip.add(subType);
218 |             }
219 |           }
220 | 
221 |           for (T newType : newTypesToSkip) {
222 |             addTypeToSkip(newType);
223 |           }
224 | 
225 |           // If there were not any new types added, we are done here.
226 |           if (types.elements().size() == originalTypesSize) {
227 |             break;
228 |           }
229 |         }
230 |       }
231 |     }

   * Tells the type system that {@code owner} may have a property named
   * {@code propertyName}. This allows the registry to keep track of what
   * types a property is defined upon.
   *
   * This is NOT the same as saying that {@code owner} must have a property

105 |   @Override
106 |   public boolean shouldTraverse(NodeTraversal t, Node n, Node parent) {
107 | 
108 |     switch (n.getType()) {
109 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
110 |         {
111 |           // Add recursive function name, if needed.
112 |           // NOTE: "enterScope" is called after we need to pick up this name.
113 |           Renamer renamer = nameStack.peek().forChildScope();
114 | 
115 |           // If needed, add the function recursive name.
116 |           String name = n.getFirstChild().getString();
117 |           if (name != null && !name.isEmpty() && parent != null
118 |               && !NodeUtil.isFunctionDeclaration(n)) {
119 |             renamer.addDeclaredName(name);
120 |           }
121 | 
122 |           nameStack.push(renamer);
123 |         }
124 |         break;
125 | 
126 |       case Token.PARAM_LIST: {
127 |           Renamer renamer = nameStack.peek().forChildScope();
128 | 
129 |           // Add the function parameters
130 |           for (Node c = n.getFirstChild(); c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
131 |             String name = c.getString();
132 |             renamer.addDeclaredName(name);
133 |           }
134 | 
135 |           // Add the function body declarations
136 |           Node functionBody = n.getNext();
137 |           findDeclaredNames(functionBody, null, renamer);
138 | 
139 |           nameStack.push(renamer);
140 |         }
141 |         break;
142 | 
143 |       case Token.CATCH:
144 |         {
145 |           Renamer renamer = nameStack.peek().forChildScope();
146 | 
147 |           String name = n.getFirstChild().getString();
148 |           renamer.addDeclaredName(name);
149 | 
150 |           nameStack.push(renamer);
151 |         }
152 |         break;
153 |     }
154 | 
155 |     return true;
156 |   }

===== M0916 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.CodeGenerator.add(Node,Context)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/CodeGenerator.java
Original range: 107-763
Documentation:

Method code:
107 |   void add(Node n, Context context) {
108 |     if (!cc.continueProcessing()) {
109 |       return;
110 |     }
111 | 
112 |     int type = n.getType();
113 |     String opstr = NodeUtil.opToStr(type);
114 |     int childCount = n.getChildCount();
115 |     Node first = n.getFirstChild();
116 |     Node last = n.getLastChild();
117 | 
118 |     // Handle all binary operators
119 |     if (opstr != null && first != last) {
120 |       Preconditions.checkState(
121 |           childCount == 2,
122 |           "Bad binary operator \"%s\": expected 2 arguments but got %s",
123 |           opstr, childCount);
124 |       int p = NodeUtil.precedence(type);
125 | 
126 |       // For right-hand-side of operations, only pass context if it's
127 |       // the IN_FOR_INIT_CLAUSE one.
128 |       Context rhsContext = getContextForNoInOperator(context);
129 | 
130 |       if (NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(n) && NodeUtil.isAssignmentOp(last)) {
131 |         // Assignments are the only right-associative binary operators
132 |         addExpr(first, p, context);
133 |         cc.addOp(opstr, true);
134 |         addExpr(last, p, rhsContext);
135 |       } else {
136 |         unrollBinaryOperator(n, type, opstr, context, rhsContext, p, p + 1);
137 |       }
138 |       return;
139 |     }
140 | 
141 |     cc.startSourceMapping(n);
142 | 
143 |     switch (type) {
144 |       case Token.TRY: {
145 |         Preconditions.checkState(first.getNext().isBlock() &&
146 |                 !first.getNext().hasMoreThanOneChild());
147 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount >= 2 && childCount <= 3);
148 | 
149 |         add("try");
150 |         add(first, Context.PRESERVE_BLOCK);
151 | 
152 |         // second child contains the catch block, or nothing if there
153 |         // isn't a catch block
154 |         Node catchblock = first.getNext().getFirstChild();
155 |         if (catchblock != null) {
156 |           add(catchblock);
157 |         }
158 | 
159 |         if (childCount == 3) {
160 |           add("finally");
161 |           add(last, Context.PRESERVE_BLOCK);
162 |         }
163 |         break;
164 |       }
165 | 
166 |       case Token.CATCH:
167 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
168 |         add("catch(");
169 |         add(first);
170 |         add(")");
171 |         add(last, Context.PRESERVE_BLOCK);
172 |         break;
173 | 
174 |       case Token.THROW:
175 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
176 |         add("throw");
177 |         add(first);
178 | 
179 |         // Must have a ';' after a throw statement, otherwise safari can't
180 |         // parse this.
181 |         cc.endStatement(true);
182 |         break;
183 | 
184 |       case Token.RETURN:
185 |         add("return");
186 |         if (childCount == 1) {
187 |           add(first);
188 |         } else {
189 |           Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
190 |         }
191 |         cc.endStatement();
192 |         break;
193 | 
194 |       case Token.VAR:
195 |         if (first != null) {
196 |           add("var ");
197 |           addList(first, false, getContextForNoInOperator(context));
198 |         }
199 |         break;
200 | 
201 |       case Token.LABEL_NAME:
202 |         Preconditions.checkState(!n.getString().isEmpty());
203 |         addIdentifier(n.getString());
204 |         break;
205 | 
206 |       case Token.NAME:
207 |         if (first == null || first.isEmpty()) {
208 |           addIdentifier(n.getString());
209 |         } else {
210 |           Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
211 |           addIdentifier(n.getString());
212 |           cc.addOp("=", true);
213 |           if (first.isComma()) {
214 |             addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(Token.ASSIGN), Context.OTHER);
215 |           } else {
216 |             // Add expression, consider nearby code at lowest level of
217 |             // precedence.
218 |             addExpr(first, 0, getContextForNoInOperator(context));
219 |           }
220 |         }
221 |         break;
222 | 
223 |       case Token.ARRAYLIT:
224 |         add("[");
225 |         addArrayList(first);
226 |         add("]");
227 |         break;
228 | 
229 |       case Token.PARAM_LIST:
230 |         add("(");
231 |         addList(first);
232 |         add(")");
233 |         break;
234 | 
235 |       case Token.COMMA:
236 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
237 |         unrollBinaryOperator(n, Token.COMMA, ",", context,
238 |             getContextForNoInOperator(context), 0, 0);
239 |         break;
240 | 
241 |       case Token.NUMBER:
242 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
243 |         cc.addNumber(n.getDouble());
244 |         break;
245 | 
246 |       case Token.TYPEOF:
247 |       case Token.VOID:
248 |       case Token.NOT:
249 |       case Token.BITNOT:
250 |       case Token.POS: {
251 |         // All of these unary operators are right-associative
252 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
253 |         cc.addOp(NodeUtil.opToStrNoFail(type), false);
254 |         addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(type), Context.OTHER);
255 |         break;
256 |       }
257 | 
258 |       case Token.NEG: {
259 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
260 | 
261 |         // It's important to our sanity checker that the code
262 |         // we print produces the same AST as the code we parse back.
263 |         // NEG is a weird case because Rhino parses "- -2" as "2".
264 |         if (n.getFirstChild().isNumber()) {
265 |           cc.addNumber(-n.getFirstChild().getDouble());
266 |         } else {
267 |           cc.addOp(NodeUtil.opToStrNoFail(type), false);
268 |           addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(type), Context.OTHER);
269 |         }
270 | 
271 |         break;
272 |       }
273 | 
274 |       case Token.HOOK: {
275 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 3);
276 |         int p = NodeUtil.precedence(type);
277 |         Context rhsContext = getContextForNoInOperator(context);
278 |         addExpr(first, p + 1, context);
279 |         cc.addOp("?", true);
280 |         addExpr(first.getNext(), 1, rhsContext);
281 |         cc.addOp(":", true);
282 |         addExpr(last, 1, rhsContext);
283 |         break;
284 |       }
285 | 
286 |       case Token.REGEXP:
287 |         if (!first.isString() ||
288 |             !last.isString()) {
289 |           throw new Error("Expected children to be strings");
290 |         }
291 | 
292 |         String regexp = regexpEscape(first.getString(), outputCharsetEncoder);
293 | 
294 |         // I only use one .add because whitespace matters
295 |         if (childCount == 2) {
296 |           add(regexp + last.getString());
297 |         } else {
298 |           Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
299 |           add(regexp);
300 |         }
301 |         break;
302 | 
303 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
304 |         if (n.getClass() != Node.class) {
305 |           throw new Error("Unexpected Node subclass.");
306 |         }
307 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 3);
308 |         boolean funcNeedsParens = (context == Context.START_OF_EXPR);
309 |         if (funcNeedsParens) {
310 |           add("(");
311 |         }
312 | 
313 |         add("function");
314 |         add(first);
315 | 
316 |         add(first.getNext());
317 |         add(last, Context.PRESERVE_BLOCK);
318 |         cc.endFunction(context == Context.STATEMENT);
319 | 
320 |         if (funcNeedsParens) {
321 |           add(")");
322 |         }
323 |         break;
324 | 
325 |       case Token.GETTER_DEF:
326 |       case Token.SETTER_DEF:
327 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.getParent().isObjectLit());
328 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
329 |         Preconditions.checkState(first.isFunction());
330 | 
331 |         // Get methods are unnamed
332 |         Preconditions.checkState(first.getFirstChild().getString().isEmpty());
333 |         if (type == Token.GETTER_DEF) {
334 |           // Get methods have no parameters.
335 |           Preconditions.checkState(!first.getChildAtIndex(1).hasChildren());
336 |           add("get ");
337 |         } else {
338 |           // Set methods have one parameter.
339 |           Preconditions.checkState(first.getChildAtIndex(1).hasOneChild());
340 |           add("set ");
341 |         }
342 | 
343 |         // The name is on the GET or SET node.
344 |         String name = n.getString();
345 |         Node fn = first;
346 |         Node parameters = fn.getChildAtIndex(1);
347 |         Node body = fn.getLastChild();
348 | 
349 |         // Add the property name.
350 |         if (!n.isQuotedString() &&
351 |             TokenStream.isJSIdentifier(name) &&
352 |             // do not encode literally any non-literal characters that were
353 |             // Unicode escaped.
354 |             NodeUtil.isLatin(name)) {
355 |           add(name);
356 |         } else {
357 |           // Determine if the string is a simple number.
358 |           double d = getSimpleNumber(name);
359 |           if (!Double.isNaN(d)) {
360 |             cc.addNumber(d);
361 |           } else {
362 |             addJsString(n);
363 |           }
364 |         }
365 | 
366 |         add(parameters);
367 |         add(body, Context.PRESERVE_BLOCK);
368 |         break;
369 | 
370 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
371 |       case Token.BLOCK: {
372 |         if (n.getClass() != Node.class) {
373 |           throw new Error("Unexpected Node subclass.");
374 |         }
375 |         boolean preserveBlock = context == Context.PRESERVE_BLOCK;
376 |         if (preserveBlock) {
377 |           cc.beginBlock();
378 |         }
379 | 
380 |         boolean preferLineBreaks =
381 |             type == Token.SCRIPT ||
382 |             (type == Token.BLOCK &&
383 |                 !preserveBlock &&
384 |                 n.getParent() != null &&
385 |                 n.getParent().isScript());
386 |         for (Node c = first; c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
387 |           add(c, Context.STATEMENT);
388 | 
389 |           // VAR doesn't include ';' since it gets used in expressions
390 |           if (c.isVar()) {
391 |             cc.endStatement();
392 |           }
393 | 
394 |           if (c.isFunction()) {
395 |             cc.maybeLineBreak();
396 |           }
397 | 
398 |           // Prefer to break lines in between top-level statements
399 |           // because top-level statements are more homogeneous.
400 |           if (preferLineBreaks) {
401 |             cc.notePreferredLineBreak();
402 |           }
403 |         }
404 |         if (preserveBlock) {
405 |           cc.endBlock(cc.breakAfterBlockFor(n, context == Context.STATEMENT));
406 |         }
407 |         break;
408 |       }
409 | 
410 |       case Token.FOR:
411 |         if (childCount == 4) {
412 |           add("for(");
413 |           if (first.isVar()) {
414 |             add(first, Context.IN_FOR_INIT_CLAUSE);
415 |           } else {
416 |             addExpr(first, 0, Context.IN_FOR_INIT_CLAUSE);
417 |           }
418 |           add(";");
419 |           add(first.getNext());
420 |           add(";");
421 |           add(first.getNext().getNext());
422 |           add(")");
423 |           addNonEmptyStatement(
424 |               last, getContextForNonEmptyExpression(context), false);
425 |         } else {
426 |           Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 3);
427 |           add("for(");
428 |           add(first);
429 |           add("in");
430 |           add(first.getNext());
431 |           add(")");
432 |           addNonEmptyStatement(
433 |               last, getContextForNonEmptyExpression(context), false);
434 |         }
435 |         break;
436 | 
437 |       case Token.DO:
438 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
439 |         add("do");
440 |         addNonEmptyStatement(first, Context.OTHER, false);
441 |         add("while(");
442 |         add(last);
443 |         add(")");
444 |         cc.endStatement();
445 |         break;
446 | 
447 |       case Token.WHILE:
448 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
449 |         add("while(");
450 |         add(first);
451 |         add(")");
452 |         addNonEmptyStatement(
453 |             last, getContextForNonEmptyExpression(context), false);
454 |         break;
455 | 
456 |       case Token.EMPTY:
457 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
458 |         break;
459 | 
460 |       case Token.GETPROP: {
461 |         Preconditions.checkState(
462 |             childCount == 2,
463 |             "Bad GETPROP: expected 2 children, but got %s", childCount);
464 |         Preconditions.checkState(
465 |             last.isString(),
466 |             "Bad GETPROP: RHS should be STRING");
467 |         boolean needsParens = (first.isNumber());
468 |         if (needsParens) {
469 |           add("(");
470 |         }
471 |         addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(type), context);
472 |         if (needsParens) {
473 |           add(")");
474 |         }
475 |         if (this.languageMode == LanguageMode.ECMASCRIPT3
476 |             && TokenStream.isKeyword(last.getString())) {
477 |           // Check for ECMASCRIPT3 keywords.
478 |           add("[");
479 |           add(last);
480 |           add("]");
481 |         } else {
482 |           add(".");
483 |           addIdentifier(last.getString());
484 |         }
485 |         break;
486 |       }
487 | 
488 |       case Token.GETELEM:
489 |         Preconditions.checkState(
490 |             childCount == 2,
491 |             "Bad GETELEM: expected 2 children but got %s", childCount);
492 |         addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(type), context);
493 |         add("[");
494 |         add(first.getNext());
495 |         add("]");
496 |         break;
497 | 
498 |       case Token.WITH:
499 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
500 |         add("with(");
501 |         add(first);
502 |         add(")");
503 |         addNonEmptyStatement(
504 |             last, getContextForNonEmptyExpression(context), false);
505 |         break;
506 | 
507 |       case Token.INC:
508 |       case Token.DEC: {
509 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
510 |         String o = type == Token.INC ? "++" : "--";
511 |         int postProp = n.getIntProp(Node.INCRDECR_PROP);
512 |         // A non-zero post-prop value indicates a post inc/dec, default of zero
513 |         // is a pre-inc/dec.
514 |         if (postProp != 0) {
515 |           addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(type), context);
516 |           cc.addOp(o, false);
517 |         } else {
518 |           cc.addOp(o, false);
519 |           add(first);
520 |         }
521 |         break;
522 |       }
523 | 
524 |       case Token.CALL:
525 |         // We have two special cases here:
526 |         // 1) If the left hand side of the call is a direct reference to eval,
527 |         // then it must have a DIRECT_EVAL annotation. If it does not, then
528 |         // that means it was originally an indirect call to eval, and that
529 |         // indirectness must be preserved.
530 |         // 2) If the left hand side of the call is a property reference,
531 |         // then the call must not a FREE_CALL annotation. If it does, then
532 |         // that means it was originally an call without an explicit this and
533 |         // that must be preserved.
534 |         if (isIndirectEval(first)
535 |             || n.getBooleanProp(Node.FREE_CALL) && NodeUtil.isGet(first)) {
536 |           add("(0,");
537 |           addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(Token.COMMA), Context.OTHER);
538 |           add(")");
539 |         } else {
540 |           addExpr(first, NodeUtil.precedence(type), context);
541 |         }
542 |         add("(");
543 |         addList(first.getNext());
544 |         add(")");
545 |         break;
546 | 
547 |       case Token.IF:
548 |         boolean hasElse = childCount == 3;
549 |         boolean ambiguousElseClause =
550 |             context == Context.BEFORE_DANGLING_ELSE && !hasElse;
551 |         if (ambiguousElseClause) {
552 |           cc.beginBlock();
553 |         }
554 | 
555 |         add("if(");
556 |         add(first);
557 |         add(")");
558 | 
559 |         if (hasElse) {
560 |           addNonEmptyStatement(
561 |               first.getNext(), Context.BEFORE_DANGLING_ELSE, false);
562 |           add("else");
563 |           addNonEmptyStatement(
564 |               last, getContextForNonEmptyExpression(context), false);
565 |         } else {
566 |           addNonEmptyStatement(first.getNext(), Context.OTHER, false);
567 |           Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
568 |         }
569 | 
570 |         if (ambiguousElseClause) {
571 |           cc.endBlock();
572 |         }
573 |         break;
574 | 
575 |       case Token.NULL:
576 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
577 |         cc.addConstant("null");
578 |         break;
579 | 
580 |       case Token.THIS:
581 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
582 |         add("this");
583 |         break;
584 | 
585 |       case Token.FALSE:
586 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
587 |         cc.addConstant("false");
588 |         break;
589 | 
590 |       case Token.TRUE:
591 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
592 |         cc.addConstant("true");
593 |         break;
594 | 
595 |       case Token.CONTINUE:
596 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount <= 1);
597 |         add("continue");
598 |         if (childCount == 1) {
599 |           if (!first.isLabelName()) {
600 |             throw new Error("Unexpected token type. Should be LABEL_NAME.");
601 |           }
602 |           add(" ");
603 |           add(first);
604 |         }
605 |         cc.endStatement();
606 |         break;
607 | 
608 |       case Token.DEBUGGER:
609 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 0);
610 |         add("debugger");
611 |         cc.endStatement();
612 |         break;
613 | 
614 |       case Token.BREAK:
615 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount <= 1);
616 |         add("break");
617 |         if (childCount == 1) {
618 |           if (!first.isLabelName()) {
619 |             throw new Error("Unexpected token type. Should be LABEL_NAME.");
620 |           }
621 |           add(" ");
622 |           add(first);
623 |         }
624 |         cc.endStatement();
625 |         break;
626 | 
627 |       case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
628 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
629 |         add(first, Context.START_OF_EXPR);
630 |         cc.endStatement();
631 |         break;
632 | 
633 |       case Token.NEW:
634 |         add("new ");
635 |         int precedence = NodeUtil.precedence(type);
636 | 
637 |         // If the first child contains a CALL, then claim higher precedence
638 |         // to force parentheses. Otherwise, when parsed, NEW will bind to the
639 |         // first viable parentheses (don't traverse into functions).
640 |         if (NodeUtil.containsType(
641 |             first, Token.CALL, NodeUtil.MATCH_NOT_FUNCTION)) {
642 |           precedence = NodeUtil.precedence(first.getType()) + 1;
643 |         }
644 |         addExpr(first, precedence, Context.OTHER);
645 | 
646 |         // '()' is optional when no arguments are present
647 |         Node next = first.getNext();
648 |         if (next != null) {
649 |           add("(");
650 |           addList(next);
651 |           add(")");
652 |         }
653 |         break;
654 | 
655 |       case Token.STRING_KEY:
656 |         Preconditions.checkState(
657 |             childCount == 1, "Object lit key must have 1 child");
658 |         addJsString(n);
659 |         break;
660 | 
661 |       case Token.STRING:
662 |         Preconditions.checkState(
663 |             childCount == 0, "A string may not have children");
664 |         addJsString(n);
665 |         break;
666 | 
667 |       case Token.DELPROP:
668 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
669 |         add("delete ");
670 |         add(first);
671 |         break;
672 | 
673 |       case Token.OBJECTLIT: {
674 |         boolean needsParens = (context == Context.START_OF_EXPR);
675 |         if (needsParens) {
676 |           add("(");
677 |         }
678 |         add("{");
679 |         for (Node c = first; c != null; c = c.getNext()) {
680 |           if (c != first) {
681 |             cc.listSeparator();
682 |           }
683 | 
684 |           if (c.isGetterDef() || c.isSetterDef()) {
685 |             add(c);
686 |           } else {
687 |             Preconditions.checkState(c.isStringKey());
688 |             String key = c.getString();
689 |             // Object literal property names don't have to be quoted if they
690 |             // are not JavaScript keywords
691 |             if (!c.isQuotedString()
692 |                 && !(languageMode == LanguageMode.ECMASCRIPT3
693 |                     && TokenStream.isKeyword(key))
694 |                 && TokenStream.isJSIdentifier(key)
695 |                 // do not encode literally any non-literal characters that
696 |                 // were Unicode escaped.
697 |                 && NodeUtil.isLatin(key)) {
698 |               add(key);
699 |             } else {
700 |               // Determine if the string is a simple number.
701 |               double d = getSimpleNumber(key);
702 |               if (!Double.isNaN(d)) {
703 |                 cc.addNumber(d);
704 |               } else {
705 |                 addExpr(c, 1, Context.OTHER);
706 |               }
707 |             }
708 |             add(":");
709 |             addExpr(c.getFirstChild(), 1, Context.OTHER);
710 |           }
711 |         }
712 |         add("}");
713 |         if (needsParens) {
714 |           add(")");
715 |         }
716 |         break;
717 |       }
718 | 
719 |       case Token.SWITCH:
720 |         add("switch(");
721 |         add(first);
722 |         add(")");
723 |         cc.beginBlock();
724 |         addAllSiblings(first.getNext());
725 |         cc.endBlock(context == Context.STATEMENT);
726 |         break;
727 | 
728 |       case Token.CASE:
729 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
730 |         add("case ");
731 |         add(first);
732 |         addCaseBody(last);
733 |         break;
734 | 
735 |       case Token.DEFAULT_CASE:
736 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 1);
737 |         add("default");
738 |         addCaseBody(first);
739 |         break;
740 | 
741 |       case Token.LABEL:
742 |         Preconditions.checkState(childCount == 2);
743 |         if (!first.isLabelName()) {
744 |           throw new Error("Unexpected token type. Should be LABEL_NAME.");
745 |         }
746 |         add(first);
747 |         add(":");
748 |         addNonEmptyStatement(
749 |             last, getContextForNonEmptyExpression(context), true);
750 |         break;
751 | 
752 |       case Token.CAST:
753 |         add("(");
754 |         add(first);
755 |         add(")");
756 |         break;
757 | 
758 |       default:
759 |         throw new Error("Unknown type " + type + "\n" + n.toStringTree());
760 |     }
761 | 
762 |     cc.endSourceMapping(n);
763 |   }

===== M0927 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.JSType.checkEquivalenceHelper(JSType,EquivalenceMethod)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/rhino/jstype/JSType.java
Original range: 570-638
Documentation:
/**
   * An equivalence visitor.
   */
Method code:
570 |   boolean checkEquivalenceHelper(JSType that, EquivalenceMethod eqMethod) {
571 |     if (this == that) {
572 |       return true;
573 |     }
574 | 
575 |     boolean thisUnknown = isUnknownType();
576 |     boolean thatUnknown = that.isUnknownType();
577 |     if (thisUnknown || thatUnknown) {
578 |       if (eqMethod == EquivalenceMethod.INVARIANT) {
579 |         // If we're checking for invariance, the unknown type is invariant
580 |         // with everyone.
581 |         return true;
582 |       } else if (eqMethod == EquivalenceMethod.DATA_FLOW) {
583 |         // If we're checking data flow, then two types are the same if they're
584 |         // both unknown.
585 |         return thisUnknown && thatUnknown;
586 |       } else if (thisUnknown && thatUnknown &&
587 |           (isNominalType() ^ that.isNominalType())) {
588 |         // If they're both unknown, but one is a nominal type and the other
589 |         // is not, then we should fail out immediately. This ensures that
590 |         // we won't unbox the unknowns further down.
591 |         return false;
592 |       }
593 |     }
594 | 
595 |     if (isUnionType() && that.isUnionType()) {
596 |       return toMaybeUnionType().checkUnionEquivalenceHelper(
597 |           that.toMaybeUnionType(), eqMethod);
598 |     }
599 | 
600 |     if (isFunctionType() && that.isFunctionType()) {
601 |       return toMaybeFunctionType().checkFunctionEquivalenceHelper(
602 |           that.toMaybeFunctionType(), eqMethod);
603 |     }
604 | 
605 |     if (isRecordType() && that.isRecordType()) {
606 |       return toMaybeRecordType().checkRecordEquivalenceHelper(
607 |           that.toMaybeRecordType(), eqMethod);
608 |     }
609 | 
610 |     if (!getTemplateTypeMap().checkEquivalenceHelper(
611 |         that.getTemplateTypeMap(), eqMethod)) {
612 |       return false;
613 |     }
614 | 
615 |     if (isNominalType() && that.isNominalType()) {
616 |       return toObjectType().getReferenceName().equals(
617 |           that.toObjectType().getReferenceName());
618 |     }
619 | 
620 |     // Unbox other proxies.
621 |     if (this instanceof ProxyObjectType) {
622 |       return ((ProxyObjectType) this)
623 |           .getReferencedTypeInternal().checkEquivalenceHelper(
624 |               that, eqMethod);
625 |     }
626 | 
627 |     if (that instanceof ProxyObjectType) {
628 |       return checkEquivalenceHelper(
629 |           ((ProxyObjectType) that).getReferencedTypeInternal(),
630 |           eqMethod);
631 |     }
632 | 
633 |     // Relies on the fact that for the base {@link JSType}, only one
634 |     // instance of each sub-type will ever be created in a given registry, so
635 |     // there is no need to verify members. If the object pointers are not
636 |     // identical, then the type member must be different.
637 |     return this == that;
638 |   }

   * Updates the scope according to the result of a type change, like
   * an assignment or a type cast.

Method code:
519 |   private void updateScopeForTypeChange(
520 |       FlowScope scope, Node left, JSType leftType, JSType resultType) {
521 |     Preconditions.checkNotNull(resultType);
522 |     switch (left.getType()) {
523 |       case Token.NAME:
524 |         String varName = left.getString();
525 |         Var var = syntacticScope.getVar(varName);
526 | 
527 |         // When looking at VAR initializers for declared VARs, we trust
528 |         // the declared type over the type it's being initialized to.
529 |         // This has two purposes:
530 |         // 1) We avoid re-declaring declared variables so that built-in
531 |         //    types defined in externs are not redeclared.
532 |         // 2) When there's a lexical closure like
533 |         //    /** @type {?string} */ var x = null;
534 |         //    function f() { x = 'xyz'; }

537 |         boolean isVarDeclaration = left.hasChildren();

539 |           redeclareSimpleVar(scope, left, resultType);
540 |         }

542 |             resultType : null);
543 | 
544 |         if (var != null && var.isTypeInferred()) {
545 |           JSType oldType = var.getType();
546 |           var.setType(oldType == null ?
547 |               resultType : oldType.getLeastSupertype(resultType));
548 |         }
549 |         break;

/**
   * Scans and gather variables declarations under a Node
   */
Method code:
123 |   private void scanVars(Node n) {
124 |     switch (n.getType()) {
125 |       case Token.VAR:
126 |         // Declare all variables. e.g. var x = 1, y, z;
127 |         for (Node child = n.getFirstChild();
128 |              child != null;) {
129 |           Node next = child.getNext();
130 |           declareVar(child);
131 |           child = next;
132 |         }
133 |         return;
134 | 
135 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
136 |         if (NodeUtil.isFunctionExpression(n)) {
137 |           return;
138 |         }
139 | 
140 |         String fnName = n.getFirstChild().getString();
141 |         if (fnName.isEmpty()) {
142 |           // This is invalid, but allow it so the checks can catch it.
143 |           return;
144 |         }
145 |         declareVar(n.getFirstChild());
146 |         return;   // should not examine function's children
147 | 
148 |       case Token.CATCH:
149 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.getChildCount() == 2);
150 |         Preconditions.checkState(n.getFirstChild().isName());
151 |         // the first child is the catch var and the third child
152 |         // is the code block
153 | 
154 |         final Node var = n.getFirstChild();
155 |         final Node block = var.getNext();
156 | 
157 |         declareVar(var);
158 |         scanVars(block);
159 |         return;  // only one child to scan
160 | 
161 |       case Token.SCRIPT:
162 |         inputId = n.getInputId();
163 |         Preconditions.checkNotNull(inputId);
164 |         break;
165 |     }
166 | 
167 |     // Variables can only occur in statement-level nodes, so
168 |     // we only need to traverse children in a couple special cases.
169 |     if (NodeUtil.isControlStructure(n) || NodeUtil.isStatementBlock(n)) {
170 |       for (Node child = n.getFirstChild();
171 |            child != null;) {
172 |         Node next = child.getNext();
173 |         scanVars(child);
174 |         child = next;
175 |       }
176 |     }

335 |   protected int getChar() {
336 |     if (ungetCursor != 0) {

356 |

380 |         }
381 |       }

===== M1022 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.shouldTraverse(NodeTraversal,Node,Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 217-292
Documentation:

Method code:
217 |   @Override
218 |   public boolean shouldTraverse(
219 |       NodeTraversal nodeTraversal, Node n, Node parent) {
220 |     astPosition.put(n, astPositionCounter++);
221 | 
222 |     switch (n.getType()) {
223 |       case Token.FUNCTION:
224 |         if (shouldTraverseFunctions || n == cfg.getEntry().getValue()) {
225 |           exceptionHandler.push(n);
226 |           return true;
227 |         }
228 |         return false;
229 |       case Token.TRY:
230 |         exceptionHandler.push(n);
231 |         return true;
232 |     }
233 | 
234 |     /*
235 |      * We are going to stop the traversal depending on what the node's parent
236 |      * is.
237 |      *
238 |      * We are only interested in adding edges between nodes that change control
239 |      * flow. The most obvious ones are loops and IF-ELSE's. A statement
240 |      * transfers control to its next sibling.
241 |      *
242 |      * In case of an expression tree, there is no control flow within the tree
243 |      * even when there are short circuited operators and conditionals. When we
244 |      * are doing data flow analysis, we will simply synthesize lattices up the
245 |      * expression tree by finding the meet at each expression node.
246 |      *
247 |      * For example: within a Token.SWITCH, the expression in question does not
248 |      * change the control flow and need not to be considered.
249 |      */
250 |     if (parent != null) {
251 |       switch (parent.getType()) {
252 |         case Token.FOR:
253 |           // Only traverse the body of the for loop.
254 |           return n == parent.getLastChild();
255 | 
256 |         // Skip the conditions.
257 |         case Token.IF:
258 |         case Token.WHILE:
259 |         case Token.WITH:
260 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
261 |         case Token.DO:
262 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild().getNext();
263 |         // Only traverse the body of the cases
264 |         case Token.SWITCH:
265 |         case Token.CASE:
266 |         case Token.CATCH:
267 |         case Token.LABEL:
268 |           return n != parent.getFirstChild();
269 |         case Token.FUNCTION:
270 |           return n == parent.getFirstChild().getNext().getNext();
271 |         case Token.CONTINUE:
272 |         case Token.BREAK:
273 |         case Token.EXPR_RESULT:
274 |         case Token.VAR:
275 |         case Token.RETURN:
276 |         case Token.THROW:
277 |           return false;
278 |         case Token.TRY:
279 |           /* Just before we are about to visit the second child of the TRY node,
280 |            * we know that we will be visiting either the CATCH or the FINALLY.
281 |            * In other words, we know that the post order traversal of the TRY
282 |            * block has been finished, no more exceptions can be caught by the
283 |            * handler at this TRY block and should be taken out of the stack.
284 |            */
285 |           if (n == parent.getFirstChild().getNext()) {
286 |             Preconditions.checkState(exceptionHandler.peek() == parent);
287 |             exceptionHandler.pop();
288 |           }
289 |       }
290 |     }
291 |     return true;
292 |   }

/**
   * Gets all the symbols that have been defined before this point
   * in the current flow. Does not return slots that have not changed during
   * the flow.
   *
   * For example, consider the code:
   * <code>
   * var x = 3;
   * function f() {
   *   var y = 5;
   *   y = 6; // FLOW POINT
   *   var z = y;
   *   return z;
   * }
   * </code>
   * A FlowScope at FLOW POINT will return a slot for y, but not
   * a slot for x or z.
   */
Method code:
346 |   private Map<String, StaticSlot<JSType>> allFlowSlots() {
347 |     Map<String, StaticSlot<JSType>> slots = Maps.newHashMap();
348 |     for (LinkedFlowSlot slot = lastSlot;
349 |          slot != null; slot = slot.parent) {
350 |       if (!slots.containsKey(slot.getName())) {
351 |         slots.put(slot.getName(), slot);
352 |       }
353 |     }
354 | 
355 |     for (Map.Entry<String, StaticSlot<JSType>> symbolEntry : cache.symbols.entrySet()) {
356 |       if (!slots.containsKey(symbolEntry.getKey())) {
357 |         slots.put(symbolEntry.getKey(), symbolEntry.getValue());
358 |       }
359 |     }
360 | 
361 |     return slots;
362 |   }

   * Adds an alternate to the union type under construction. Returns this
   * for easy chaining.

122 |     // just bail out early here.
123 |     if (alternate.isNoType()) {
124 |       return this;
125 |     }
126 |

128 |

131 |     if (isAlternateUnknown) {
132 |       areAllUnknownsChecked = areAllUnknownsChecked &&
133 |           alternate.isCheckedUnknownType();
134 |     }
135 |     if (!isAllType && !isNativeUnknownType) {
136 |       if (alternate.isUnionType()) {
137 |         UnionType union = alternate.toMaybeUnionType();
138 |         for (JSType unionAlt : union.getAlternates()) {
139 |           addAlternate(unionAlt);
140 |         }
141 |       } else {
142 |         if (alternates.size() > maxUnionSize) {
143 |           return this;
144 |         }
145 | 
146 |         // Function types are special, because they have their
147 |         // own bizarre sub-lattice. See the comments on
148 |         // FunctionType#supAndInf helper and above at functionTypePosition.
149 |         if (alternate.isFunctionType() && functionTypePosition != -1) {
150 |           // See the comments on functionTypePosition above.
151 |           FunctionType other =
152 |               alternates.get(functionTypePosition).toMaybeFunctionType();
153 |           FunctionType supremum =
154 |               alternate.toMaybeFunctionType().supAndInfHelper(other, true);
155 |           alternates.set(functionTypePosition, supremum);
156 |           result = null;
157 |           return this;
158 |         }
159 | 
160 |         // Look through the alternates we've got so far,
161 |         // and check if any of them are duplicates of
162 |         // one another.
163 |         int currentIndex = 0;
164 |         Iterator<JSType> it = alternates.iterator();
165 |         while (it.hasNext()) {
166 |           boolean removeCurrent = false;
167 |           JSType current = it.next();
168 | 
169 |           // Unknown and NoResolved types may just be names that haven't
170 |           // been resolved yet. So keep these in the union, and just use
171 |           // equality checking for simple de-duping.
172 |           if (alternate.isUnknownType() ||
173 |               current.isUnknownType() ||
174 |               alternate.isNoResolvedType() ||
175 |               current.isNoResolvedType() ||
176 |               alternate.hasAnyTemplateTypes() ||
177 |               current.hasAnyTemplateTypes()) {
178 |             if (alternate.isEquivalentTo(current)) {
179 |               // Alternate is unnecessary.
180 |               return this;
181 |             }
182 |           } else {
183 | 
184 |             // Because "Foo" and "Foo.<?>" are roughly equivalent
185 |             // templatized types, special care is needed when building the
186 |             // union. For example:
187 |             //   Object is consider a subtype of Object.<string>
188 |             // but we want to leave "Object" not "Object.<string>" when
189 |             // building the subtype.
190 |             //
191 | 
192 |             if (alternate.isTemplatizedType() || current.isTemplatizedType()) {
193 |               // Cases:
194 |               // 1) alternate:Array.<string> and current:Object ==> Object
195 |               // 2) alternate:Array.<string> and current:Array ==> Array
196 |               // 3) alternate:Object.<string> and
197 |               //    current:Array ==> Array|Object.<string>
198 |               // 4) alternate:Object and current:Array.<string> ==> Object
199 |               // 5) alternate:Array and current:Array.<string> ==> Array
200 |               // 6) alternate:Array and
201 |               //    current:Object.<string> ==> Array|Object.<string>
202 |               // 7) alternate:Array.<string> and
203 |               //    current:Array.<number> ==> Array.<?>
204 |               // 8) alternate:Array.<string> and
205 |               //    current:Array.<string> ==> Array.<string>
206 |               // 9) alternate:Array.<string> and
207 |               //    current:Object.<string> ==> Object.<string>|Array.<string>
208 | 
209 |               if (!current.isTemplatizedType()) {
210 |                 if (alternate.isSubtype(current)) {
211 |                   // case 1, 2
212 |                   return this;
213 |                 }
214 |                 // case 3: leave current, add alternate
215 |               } else if (!alternate.isTemplatizedType()) {
216 |                 if (current.isSubtype(alternate)) {
217 |                   // case 4, 5
218 |                   removeCurrent = true;
219 |                 }
220 |                 // case 6: leave current, add alternate
221 |               } else {
222 |                 Preconditions.checkState(current.isTemplatizedType()
223 |                     && alternate.isTemplatizedType());
224 |                 TemplatizedType templatizedAlternate = alternate.toMaybeTemplatizedType();
225 |                 TemplatizedType templatizedCurrent = current.toMaybeTemplatizedType();
226 | 
227 |                 if (templatizedCurrent.wrapsSameRawType(templatizedAlternate)) {
228 |                   if (alternate.getTemplateTypeMap().checkEquivalenceHelper(
229 |                       current.getTemplateTypeMap(),
230 |                       EquivalenceMethod.IDENTITY)) {
231 |                     // case 8
232 |                     return this;
233 |                   } else {
234 |                     // TODO(johnlenz): should we leave both types?
235 |                     // case 7: add a merged alternate
236 |                     // We currently merge to the templatized types to "unknown"
237 |                     // which is equivalent to the raw type.
238 |                     JSType merged = templatizedCurrent
239 |                         .getReferencedObjTypeInternal();
240 |                     return addAlternate(merged);
241 |                   }
242 |                 }
243 |                 // case 9: leave current, add alternate
244 |               }
245 |               // Otherwise leave both templatized types.
246 |             } else if (alternate.isSubtype(current)) {
247 |               // Alternate is unnecessary.
248 |               return this;
249 |             } else if (current.isSubtype(alternate)) {
250 |               // Alternate makes current obsolete
251 |               removeCurrent = true;
252 |             }
253 |           }
254 | 
255 |           if (removeCurrent) {
256 |             it.remove();
257 | 
258 |             if (currentIndex == functionTypePosition) {
259 |               functionTypePosition = -1;
260 |             } else if (currentIndex < functionTypePosition) {
261 |               functionTypePosition--;
262 |               currentIndex--;
263 |             }
264 |           }
265 |           currentIndex++;
266 |         }
267 | 
268 |         if (alternate.isFunctionType()) {
269 |           // See the comments on functionTypePosition above.
270 |           Preconditions.checkState(functionTypePosition == -1);
271 |           functionTypePosition = alternates.size();
272 |         }
273 | 
274 |         alternates.add(alternate);
275 |         result = null; // invalidate the memoized result
276 |       }
277 |     } else {
278 |       result = null;
279 |     }
280 |     return this;
281 |   }

/**
   * Visits the parameters of a CALL or a NEW node.
   */
Method code:
1828 |   private void visitParameterList(NodeTraversal t, Node call,
1829 |       FunctionType functionType) {
1830 |     Iterator<Node> arguments = call.children().iterator();
1831 |     arguments.next(); // skip the function name
1832 | 
1833 |     Iterator<Node> parameters = functionType.getParameters().iterator();
1834 |     int ordinal = 0;
1835 |     Node parameter = null;
1836 |     Node argument = null;
1837 |     while (arguments.hasNext() &&
1838 |            (parameters.hasNext() ||
1839 |             parameter != null && parameter.isVarArgs())) {
1840 |       // If there are no parameters left in the list, then the while loop
1841 |       // above implies that this must be a var_args function.
1842 |       if (parameters.hasNext()) {
1843 |         parameter = parameters.next();
1844 |       }
1845 |       argument = arguments.next();
1846 |       ordinal++;
1847 | 
1848 |       validator.expectArgumentMatchesParameter(t, argument,
1849 |           getJSType(argument), getJSType(parameter), call, ordinal);
1850 |     }
1851 | 
1852 |     int numArgs = call.getChildCount() - 1;
1853 |     int minArgs = functionType.getMinArguments();
1854 |     int maxArgs = functionType.getMaxArguments();
1855 |     if (minArgs > numArgs || maxArgs < numArgs) {
1856 |       report(t, call, WRONG_ARGUMENT_COUNT,
1857 |               validator.getReadableJSTypeName(call.getFirstChild(), false),
1858 |               String.valueOf(numArgs), String.valueOf(minArgs),
1859 |               maxArgs != Integer.MAX_VALUE ?
1860 |               " and no more than " + maxArgs + " argument(s)" : "");
1861 |     }
1862 |   }
