/**
   * {@inheritDoc}
   *
   * <p>This enforces the Google const name convention, that the first character
   * after the last $ must be an upper-case letter and all subsequent letters
   * must be upper case. The name must be at least 2 characters long.
   *
   * <p>Examples:
   * <pre>
   *      aaa          Not constant - lower-case letters in the name
   *      A            Not constant - too short
   *      goog$A       Constant - letters after the $ are upper-case.
   *      AA17         Constant - digits can appear after the first letter
   *      goog$7A      Not constant - first character after the $ must be
   *                   upper case.
   *      $A           Constant - doesn't have to be anything in front of the $
   * </pre>
   */
Method code:
70 |   @Override
71 |   public boolean isConstant(String name) {
72 |     if (name.length() <= 1) {
73 |       return false;
74 |     }
75 | 
76 |     // In compiled code, '$' is often a namespace delimiter. To allow inlining
77 |     // of namespaced constants, we strip off any namespaces here.
78 |     int pos = name.lastIndexOf('$');
79 |     if (pos >= 0) {
80 |       name = name.substring(pos + 1);
81 |       if (name.length() == 0) {
82 |         return false;
83 |       }
84 |     }
85 | 
86 |     return isConstantKey(name);
87 |   }

1028 |     if (that.isFunctionType()) {
1029 |       FunctionType other = that.toMaybeFunctionType();
1030 |       if (other.isInterface()) {
1031 |         // Any function can be assigned to an interface function.
1032 |         return true;
1033 |       }
1034 |       if (isInterface()) {
1035 |         // An interface function cannot be assigned to anything.
1036 |         return false;
1037 |       }
1038 | 
1039 |       // If functionA is a subtype of functionB, then their "this" types
1040 |       // should be contravariant. However, this causes problems because
1041 |       // of the way we enforce overrides. Because function(this:SubFoo)
1042 |       // is not a subtype of function(this:Foo), our override check treats
1043 |       // this as an error. Let's punt on all this for now.
1044 |       // TODO(nicksantos): fix this.
1045 |       boolean treatThisTypesAsCovariant =
1046 |         // An interface 'this'-type is non-restrictive.
1047 |         // In practical terms, if C implements I, and I has a method m,
1048 |         // then any m doesn't necessarily have to C#m's 'this'
1049 |         // type doesn't need to match I.
1050 |         (other.typeOfThis.toObjectType() != null &&
1051 |              other.typeOfThis.toObjectType().getConstructor() != null &&
1052 |              other.typeOfThis.toObjectType().getConstructor().isInterface()) ||
1053 | 
1054 |         // If one of the 'this' types is covariant of the other,
1055 |         // then we'll treat them as covariant (see comment above).
1056 |         other.typeOfThis.isSubtype(this.typeOfThis) ||
1057 |         this.typeOfThis.isSubtype(other.typeOfThis);
1058 |       return treatThisTypesAsCovariant && this.call.isSubtype(other.call);
1059 |     }
1060 | 
1061 |     return getNativeType(JSTypeNative.FUNCTION_PROTOTYPE).isSubtype(that);
1062 |   }

209 |   void addOp(String op, boolean binOp) {
210 |     maybeEndStatement();
211 | 
212 |     char first = op.charAt(0);
213 |     char prev = getLastChar();
214 | 
215 |     if ((first == '+' || first == '-') && prev == first) {
216 |       // This is not pretty printing. This is to prevent misparsing of
217 |       // things like "x + ++y" or "x++ + ++y"
218 |       append(" ");

226 |     }
227 |

232 |     // operator on the other hand is not. We only line break after a bin op

   * Expect that the first type can be addressed with GETELEM syntax,
   * and that the second type is the right type for an index into the
   * first type.
   *
   * @param t The node traversal.
   * @param n The GETELEM node to issue warnings on.

   * @param indexType The type inside the brackets of the GETELEM.
   */
Method code:
325 |   void expectIndexMatch(NodeTraversal t, Node n, JSType objType,
326 |                         JSType indexType) {
327 |     Preconditions.checkState(n.isGetElem());
328 |     Node indexNode = n.getLastChild();
329 |     if (objType.isStruct()) {
330 |       report(JSError.make(t.getSourceName(), indexNode,
331 |                           ILLEGAL_PROPERTY_ACCESS, "'[]'", "struct"));
332 |     }

342 |             "restricted index type");
343 |       } else if (dereferenced != null && dereferenced.isArrayType()) {
344 |         expectNumber(t, indexNode, indexType, "array access");
345 |       } else if (objType.matchesObjectContext()) {
346 |         expectString(t, indexNode, indexType, "property access");
347 |       } else {

349 |             objType,

/**
   * Connects cfgNode to the proper CATCH block if target subtree might throw
   * an exception. If there are FINALLY blocks reached before a CATCH, it will
   * make the corresponding entry in finallyMap.
   */
Method code:
830 |   private void connectToPossibleExceptionHandler(Node cfgNode, Node target) {
831 |     if (mayThrowException(target) && !exceptionHandler.isEmpty()) {
832 |       Node lastJump = cfgNode;
833 |       for (Node handler : exceptionHandler) {
834 |         if (handler.isFunction()) {
835 |           return;
836 |         }
837 |         Preconditions.checkState(handler.isTry());
838 |         Node catchBlock = NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(handler);
839 | 
840 |         if (!NodeUtil.hasCatchHandler(catchBlock)) { // No catch but a FINALLY.
841 |           if (lastJump == cfgNode) {
842 |             createEdge(cfgNode, Branch.ON_EX, handler.getLastChild());
843 |           } else {
844 |             finallyMap.put(lastJump, handler.getLastChild());
845 |           }
846 |         } else { // Has a catch.
847 |           if (lastJump == cfgNode) {
848 |             createEdge(cfgNode, Branch.ON_EX, catchBlock);
849 |             return;
850 |           } else {
851 |             finallyMap.put(lastJump, catchBlock);
852 |           }
853 |         }
854 |         lastJump = handler;
855 |       }
856 |     }

===== M1180 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeInferencePass.inferAllScopes(Node)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/TypeInferencePass.java
Original range: 77-112
Documentation:
/** Entry point for type inference when running over part of the tree. */
Method code:
77 |   void inferAllScopes(Node node) {
78 |     // Type analysis happens in two major phases.
79 |     // 1) Finding all the symbols.
80 |     // 2) Propagating all the inferred types.
81 |     //
82 |     // The order of this analysis is non-obvious. In a complete inference
83 |     // system, we may need to backtrack arbitrarily far. But the compile-time
84 |     // costs would be unacceptable.
85 |     //
86 |     // We do one pass where we do typed scope creation for all scopes
87 |     // in pre-order.
88 |     //
89 |     // Then we do a second pass where we do all type inference
90 |     // (type propagation) in pre-order.
91 |     //
92 |     // We use a memoized scope creator so that we never create a scope
93 |     // more than once.
94 |     //
95 |     // This will allow us to handle cases like:
96 |     // var ns = {};
97 |     // (function() { /** JSDoc */ ns.method = function() {}; })();
98 |     // ns.method();
99 |     // In this code, we need to build the symbol table for the inner scope in
100 |     // order to propagate the type of ns.method in the outer scope.
101 |     (new NodeTraversal(
102 |         compiler, new FirstScopeBuildingCallback(), scopeCreator))
103 |         .traverseWithScope(node, topScope);
104 | 
105 |     for (Scope s : scopeCreator.getAllMemoizedScopes()) {
106 |       s.resolveTypes();
107 |     }
108 | 
109 |     (new NodeTraversal(
110 |         compiler, new SecondScopeBuildingCallback(), scopeCreator))
111 |         .traverseWithScope(node, topScope);
112 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeInference.branchedFlowThrough(Node,FlowScope)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/TypeInference.java
Original range: 190-303
Documentation:

Method code:
190 |   @Override
191 |   @SuppressWarnings({"fallthrough", "incomplete-switch"})
192 |   List<FlowScope> branchedFlowThrough(Node source, FlowScope input) {
193 |     // NOTE(nicksantos): Right now, we just treat ON_EX edges like UNCOND
194 |     // edges. If we wanted to be perfect, we'd actually JOIN all the out
195 |     // lattices of this flow with the in lattice, and then make that the out
196 |     // lattice for the ON_EX edge. But it's probably too expensive to be
197 |     // worthwhile.
198 |     FlowScope output = flowThrough(source, input);
199 |     Node condition = null;
200 |     FlowScope conditionFlowScope = null;
201 |     BooleanOutcomePair conditionOutcomes = null;
202 | 
203 |     List<DiGraphEdge<Node, Branch>> branchEdges = getCfg().getOutEdges(source);
204 |     List<FlowScope> result = Lists.newArrayListWithCapacity(branchEdges.size());
205 |     for (DiGraphEdge<Node, Branch> branchEdge : branchEdges) {
206 |       Branch branch = branchEdge.getValue();
207 |       FlowScope newScope = output;
208 | 
209 |       switch (branch) {
210 |         case ON_TRUE:
211 |           if (NodeUtil.isForIn(source)) {
212 |             // item is assigned a property name, so its type should be string.
213 |             Node item = source.getFirstChild();
214 |             Node obj = item.getNext();
215 | 
216 |             FlowScope informed = traverse(obj, output.createChildFlowScope());
217 | 
218 |             if (item.isVar()) {
219 |               item = item.getFirstChild();
220 |             }
221 |             if (item.isName()) {
222 |               JSType iterKeyType = getNativeType(STRING_TYPE);
223 |               ObjectType objType = getJSType(obj).dereference();
224 |               JSType objIndexType = objType == null ?
225 |                   null : objType.getTemplateTypeMap().getTemplateType(
226 |                       registry.getObjectIndexKey());
227 |               if (objIndexType != null && !objIndexType.isUnknownType()) {
228 |                 JSType narrowedKeyType =
229 |                     iterKeyType.getGreatestSubtype(objIndexType);
230 |                 if (!narrowedKeyType.isEmptyType()) {
231 |                   iterKeyType = narrowedKeyType;
232 |                 }
233 |               }
234 |               redeclareSimpleVar(informed, item, iterKeyType);
235 |             }
236 |             newScope = informed;
237 |             break;
238 |           }
239 | 
240 |           // FALL THROUGH
241 | 
242 |         case ON_FALSE:
243 |           if (condition == null) {
244 |             condition = NodeUtil.getConditionExpression(source);
245 |             if (condition == null && source.isCase()) {
246 |               condition = source;
247 | 
248 |               // conditionFlowScope is cached from previous iterations
249 |               // of the loop.
250 |               if (conditionFlowScope == null) {
251 |                 conditionFlowScope = traverse(
252 |                     condition.getFirstChild(), output.createChildFlowScope());
253 |               }
254 |             }
255 |           }
256 | 
257 |           if (condition != null) {
258 |             if (condition.isAnd() ||
259 |                 condition.isOr()) {
260 |               // When handling the short-circuiting binary operators,
261 |               // the outcome scope on true can be different than the outcome
262 |               // scope on false.
263 |               //
264 |               // TODO(nicksantos): The "right" way to do this is to
265 |               // carry the known outcome all the way through the
266 |               // recursive traversal, so that we can construct a
267 |               // different flow scope based on the outcome. However,
268 |               // this would require a bunch of code and a bunch of
269 |               // extra computation for an edge case. This seems to be
270 |               // a "good enough" approximation.
271 | 
272 |               // conditionOutcomes is cached from previous iterations
273 |               // of the loop.
274 |               if (conditionOutcomes == null) {
275 |                 conditionOutcomes = condition.isAnd() ?
276 |                     traverseAnd(condition, output.createChildFlowScope()) :
277 |                     traverseOr(condition, output.createChildFlowScope());
278 |               }
279 |               newScope =
280 |                   reverseInterpreter.getPreciserScopeKnowingConditionOutcome(
281 |                       condition,
282 |                       conditionOutcomes.getOutcomeFlowScope(
283 |                           condition.getType(), branch == Branch.ON_TRUE),
284 |                       branch == Branch.ON_TRUE);
285 |             } else {
286 |               // conditionFlowScope is cached from previous iterations
287 |               // of the loop.
288 |               if (conditionFlowScope == null) {
289 |                 conditionFlowScope =
290 |                     traverse(condition, output.createChildFlowScope());
291 |               }
292 |               newScope =
293 |                   reverseInterpreter.getPreciserScopeKnowingConditionOutcome(
294 |                       condition, conditionFlowScope, branch == Branch.ON_TRUE);
295 |             }
296 |           }
297 |           break;
298 |       }
299 | 
300 |       result.add(newScope.optimize());
301 |     }
302 |     return result;
303 |   }

519 |       sourceName = getSourceName(n);
520 |     }
521 | 
522 |     curNode = n;
523 |     if (!callback.shouldTraverse(this, n, parent)) {
524 |       return;
525 |     }
526 | 
527 |     if (type == Token.FUNCTION) {
528 |       traverseFunction(n, parent);
529 |     } else {
530 |       for (Node child = n.getFirstChild(); child != null; ) {
531 |         // child could be replaced, in which case our child node
532 |         // would no longer point to the true next
533 |         Node next = child.getNext();
534 |         traverseBranch(child, n);
535 |         child = next;
536 |       }
537 |     }
538 | 
539 |     curNode = n;
540 |     callback.visit(this, n, parent);
541 |   }

/**
     * Creates a new function type, based on the given nodes.
     *
     * This handles two cases that are semantically very different, but
     * are not mutually exclusive:
     * - A function literal that needs a type attached to it.
     * - An assignment expression with function-type info in the JsDoc.
     *
     * All parameters are optional, and we will do the best we can to create
     * a function type.
     *
     * This function will always create a function type, so only call it if
     * you're sure that's what you want.
     *
     * @param rValue The function node.
     * @param name the function's name
     * @param info the {@link JSDocInfo} attached to the function definition
     * @param lvalueNode The node where this function is being
     *     assigned. For example, {@code A.prototype.foo = ...} would be used to
     *     determine that this function is a method of A.prototype. May be
     *     null to indicate that this is not being assigned to a qualified name.
     */

874 |         @Nullable Node rValue,

880 |

884 |         if (var != null && var.getType() != null &&

910 |           type = type.restrictByNotNullOrUndefined();

914 |           }

/**
     * Look for a type declaration on a property assignment
     * (in an ASSIGN or an object literal key).
     * @param info The doc info for this property.

     * @param rValue The node that {@code n} is being initialized to,
     *     or {@code null} if this is a stub declaration.

Method code:
1325 |     private JSType getDeclaredType(JSDocInfo info, Node lValue,
1326 |         @Nullable Node rValue) {
1327 |       if (info != null && info.hasType()) {
1328 |         return getDeclaredTypeInAnnotation(lValue, info);
1329 |       } else if (rValue != null && rValue.isFunction() &&
1330 |           shouldUseFunctionLiteralType(

1728 |           }

1731 |           }
1732 |         }

1735 |       }

1743 |                           "interface", functionPrivateName));
1744 |         }

1078 |     Node processStringLiteral(StringLiteral literalNode) {
1079 |       String value = literalNode.getValue();
1080 |       Node n = newStringNode(value);
1081 |       if (value.indexOf('\u000B') != -1) {
1082 |         // NOTE(nicksantos): In JavaScript, there are 3 ways to
1083 |         // represent a vertical tab: \v, \x0B, \u000B.
1084 |         // The \v notation was added later, and is not understood
1085 |         // on IE. So we need to preserve it as-is. This is really
1086 |         // obnoxious, because we do not have a good way to represent
1087 |         // how the original string was encoded without making the
1088 |         // representation of strings much more complicated.
1089 |         //
1090 |         // To handle this, we look at the original source test, and
1091 |         // mark the string as \v-encoded or not. If a string is
1092 |         // \v encoded, then all the vertical tabs in that string
1093 |         // will be encoded with a \v.
1094 |         int start = literalNode.getAbsolutePosition();
1095 |         int end = start + literalNode.getLength();
1096 |         if (start < sourceString.length() &&
1097 |             (sourceString.substring(
1098 |                  start, Math.min(sourceString.length(), end))
1099 |              .indexOf("\\v") != -1)) {
1100 |           n.putBooleanProp(Node.SLASH_V, true);
1101 |         }
1102 |       }
1103 |       return n;
1104 |     }

Method code:
854 |     @Override public ObjectType getTypeWithProperty(String field, JSType type) {
855 |       if (type == null) {
856 |         return null;
857 |       }
858 | 
859 |       if (type.isEnumElementType()) {
860 |         return getTypeWithProperty(
861 |             field, type.toMaybeEnumElementType().getPrimitiveType());
862 |       }
863 | 
864 |       if (!(type instanceof ObjectType)) {
865 |         if (type.autoboxesTo() != null) {
866 |           type = type.autoboxesTo();
867 |         } else {
868 |           return null;
869 |         }
870 |       }
871 | 
872 |       // Ignore the prototype itself at all times.
873 |       if ("prototype".equals(field)) {
874 |         return null;
875 |       }
876 | 
877 |       // We look up the prototype chain to find the highest place (if any) that
878 |       // this appears.  This will make references to overridden properties look
879 |       // like references to the initial property, so they are renamed alike.
880 |       ObjectType foundType = null;
881 |       ObjectType objType = ObjectType.cast(type);
882 |       if (objType != null && objType.getConstructor() != null
883 |           && objType.getConstructor().isInterface()) {
884 |         ObjectType topInterface = FunctionType.getTopDefiningInterface(
885 |             objType, field);
886 |         if (topInterface != null && topInterface.getConstructor() != null) {
887 |           foundType = topInterface.getConstructor().getPrototype();
888 |         }
889 |       } else {
890 |         while (objType != null && objType.getImplicitPrototype() != objType) {
891 |           if (objType.hasOwnProperty(field)) {
892 |             foundType = objType;
893 |           }
894 |           objType = objType.getImplicitPrototype();
895 |         }
896 |       }
897 | 
898 |       // If the property does not exist on the referenced type but the original
899 |       // type is an object type, see if any subtype has the property.
900 |       if (foundType == null) {
901 |         ObjectType maybeType = ObjectType.cast(
902 |             registry.getGreatestSubtypeWithProperty(type, field));
903 |         // getGreatestSubtypeWithProperty does not guarantee that the property
904 |         // is defined on the returned type, it just indicates that it might be,
905 |         // so we have to double check.
906 |         if (maybeType != null && maybeType.hasOwnProperty(field)) {
907 |           foundType = maybeType;
908 |         }
909 |       }
910 |       return foundType;
911 |     }

   * <code>lvalue</code> is a prototype modification, we change the schema

===== M1251 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.ControlFlowAnalysis.computeFollowNode(Node,Node,ControlFlowAnalysis)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/ControlFlowAnalysis.java
Original range: 692-789
Documentation:
/**
   * Computes the follow() node of a given node and its parent. There is a side
   * effect when calling this function. If this function computed an edge that
   * exists a FINALLY, it'll attempt to connect the fromNode to the outer
   * FINALLY according to the finallyMap.
   *
   * @param fromNode The original source node since {@code node} is changed
   *        during recursion.
   * @param node The node that follow() should compute.
   */
Method code:
692 |   private static Node computeFollowNode(
693 |       Node fromNode, Node node, ControlFlowAnalysis cfa) {
694 |     /*
695 |      * This is the case where:
696 |      *
697 |      * 1. Parent is null implies that we are transferring control to the end of
698 |      * the script.
699 |      *
700 |      * 2. Parent is a function implies that we are transferring control back to
701 |      * the caller of the function.
702 |      *
703 |      * 3. If the node is a return statement, we should also transfer control
704 |      * back to the caller of the function.
705 |      *
706 |      * 4. If the node is root then we have reached the end of what we have been
707 |      * asked to traverse.
708 |      *
709 |      * In all cases we should transfer control to a "symbolic return" node.
710 |      * This will make life easier for DFAs.
711 |      */
712 |     Node parent = node.getParent();
713 |     if (parent == null || parent.isFunction() ||
714 |         (cfa != null && node == cfa.root)) {
715 |       return null;
716 |     }
717 | 
718 |     // If we are just before a IF/WHILE/DO/FOR:
719 |     switch (parent.getType()) {
720 |       // The follow() of any of the path from IF would be what follows IF.
721 |       case Token.IF:
722 |         return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
723 |       case Token.CASE:
724 |       case Token.DEFAULT_CASE:
725 |         // After the body of a CASE, the control goes to the body of the next
726 |         // case, without having to go to the case condition.
727 |         if (parent.getNext() != null) {
728 |           if (parent.getNext().isCase()) {
729 |             return parent.getNext().getFirstChild().getNext();
730 |           } else if (parent.getNext().isDefaultCase()) {
731 |             return parent.getNext().getFirstChild();
732 |           } else {
733 |             Preconditions.checkState(false, "Not reachable");
734 |           }
735 |         } else {
736 |           return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
737 |         }
738 |         break;
739 |       case Token.FOR:
740 |         if (NodeUtil.isForIn(parent)) {
741 |           return parent;
742 |         } else {
743 |           return parent.getFirstChild().getNext().getNext();
744 |         }
745 |       case Token.WHILE:
746 |       case Token.DO:
747 |         return parent;
748 |       case Token.TRY:
749 |         // If we are coming out of the TRY block...
750 |         if (parent.getFirstChild() == node) {
751 |           if (NodeUtil.hasFinally(parent)) { // and have FINALLY block.
752 |             return computeFallThrough(parent.getLastChild());
753 |           } else { // and have no FINALLY.
754 |             return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
755 |           }
756 |         // CATCH block.
757 |         } else if (NodeUtil.getCatchBlock(parent) == node){
758 |           if (NodeUtil.hasFinally(parent)) { // and have FINALLY block.
759 |             return computeFallThrough(node.getNext());
760 |           } else {
761 |             return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
762 |           }
763 |         // If we are coming out of the FINALLY block...
764 |         } else if (parent.getLastChild() == node){
765 |           if (cfa != null) {
766 |             for (Node finallyNode : cfa.finallyMap.get(parent)) {
767 |               cfa.createEdge(fromNode, Branch.ON_EX, finallyNode);
768 |             }
769 |           }
770 |           return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
771 |         }
772 |     }
773 | 
774 |     // Now that we are done with the special cases follow should be its
775 |     // immediate sibling, unless its sibling is a function
776 |     Node nextSibling = node.getNext();
777 | 
778 |     // Skip function declarations because control doesn't get pass into it.
779 |     while (nextSibling != null && nextSibling.isFunction()) {
780 |       nextSibling = nextSibling.getNext();
781 |     }
782 | 
783 |     if (nextSibling != null) {
784 |       return computeFallThrough(nextSibling);
785 |     } else {
786 |       // If there are no more siblings, control is transferred up the AST.
787 |       return computeFollowNode(fromNode, parent, cfa);
788 |     }
789 |   }

/**
     * Declare the symbol for a qualified name in the global scope.
     *
     * @param info The doc info for this property.
     * @param n A top-level GETPROP node (it should not be contained inside
     *     another GETPROP).
     * @param parent The parent of {@code n}.
     * @param rhsValue The node that {@code n} is being initialized to,
     *     or {@code null} if this is a stub declaration.
     */
Method code:
1526 |     void maybeDeclareQualifiedName(NodeTraversal t, JSDocInfo info,
1527 |         Node n, Node parent, Node rhsValue) {
1528 |       Node ownerNode = n.getFirstChild();
1529 |       String ownerName = ownerNode.getQualifiedName();
1530 |       String qName = n.getQualifiedName();
1531 |       String propName = n.getLastChild().getString();
1532 |       Preconditions.checkArgument(qName != null && ownerName != null);
1533 | 
1534 |       // Precedence of type information on GETPROPs:
1535 |       // 1) @type annotation / @enum annotation
1536 |       // 2) ASSIGN to FUNCTION literal
1537 |       // 3) @param/@return annotation (with no function literal)
1538 |       // 4) ASSIGN to something marked @const
1539 |       // 5) ASSIGN to anything else
1540 |       //
1541 |       // 1, 3, and 4 are declarations, 5 is inferred, and 2 is a declaration iff
1542 |       // the function has JsDoc or has not been declared before.
1543 |       //
1544 |       // FUNCTION literals are special because TypedScopeCreator is very smart
1545 |       // about getting as much type information as possible for them.
1546 | 
1547 |       // Determining type for #1 + #2 + #3 + #4
1548 |       JSType valueType = getDeclaredType(info, n, rhsValue);
1549 |       if (valueType == null && rhsValue != null) {
1550 |         // Determining type for #5
1551 |         valueType = rhsValue.getJSType();
1552 |       }
1553 | 
1554 |       // Function prototypes are special.
1555 |       // It's a common JS idiom to do:
1556 |       // F.prototype = { ... };
1557 |       // So if F does not have an explicitly declared super type,
1558 |       // allow F.prototype to be redefined arbitrarily.
1559 |       if ("prototype".equals(propName)) {
1560 |         Var qVar = scope.getVar(qName);
1561 |         if (qVar != null) {

1563 |           // and they assign F.prototype to an object literal,
1564 |           // then they are responsible for making sure that the object literal's
1565 |           // implicit prototype is set up appropriately. We just obey
1566 |           // the @extends tag.
1567 |           ObjectType qVarType = ObjectType.cast(qVar.getType());
1568 |           if (qVarType != null &&
1569 |               rhsValue != null &&
1570 |               rhsValue.isObjectLit()) {
1571 |             typeRegistry.resetImplicitPrototype(
1572 |                 rhsValue.getJSType(), qVarType.getImplicitPrototype());
1573 |           } else if (!qVar.isTypeInferred()) {
1574 |             // If the programmer has declared that F inherits from Super,
1575 |             // and they assign F.prototype to some arbitrary expression,
1576 |             // there's not much we can do. We just ignore the expression,
1577 |             // and hope they've annotated their code in a way to tell us
1578 |             // what props are going to be on that prototype.
1579 |             return;
1580 |           }
1581 | 
1582 |           qVar.getScope().undeclare(qVar);
1583 |         }
1584 |       }
1585 | 
1586 |       if (valueType == null) {
1587 |         if (parent.isExprResult()) {
1588 |           stubDeclarations.add(new StubDeclaration(
1589 |               n,
1590 |               t.getInput() != null && t.getInput().isExtern(),
1591 |               ownerName));
1592 |         }
1593 | 
1594 |         return;
1595 |       }
1596 |

1599 |       if (!inferred) {
1600 |         ObjectType ownerType = getObjectSlot(ownerName);
1601 |         if (ownerType != null) {
1602 |           // Only declare this as an official property if it has not been
1603 |           // declared yet.
1604 |           boolean isExtern = t.getInput() != null && t.getInput().isExtern();
1605 |           if ((!ownerType.hasOwnProperty(propName) ||
1606 |                ownerType.isPropertyTypeInferred(propName)) &&

1608 |                !ownerType.isInstanceType())) {
1609 |             // If the property is undeclared or inferred, declare it now.
1610 |             ownerType.defineDeclaredProperty(propName, valueType, n);

1615 |         // caught when we try to declare it in the current scope.
1616 |         defineSlot(n, parent, valueType, inferred);
1617 |       } else if (rhsValue != null && rhsValue.isTrue()) {
1618 |         // We declare these for delegate proxy method properties.
1619 |         ObjectType ownerType = getObjectSlot(ownerName);
1620 |         FunctionType ownerFnType = JSType.toMaybeFunctionType(ownerType);
1621 |         if (ownerFnType != null) {

===== M1274 =====
Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.FunctionTypeBuilder.buildAndRegister()
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/FunctionTypeBuilder.java
Original range: 652-714
Documentation:
/**
   * Builds the function type, and puts it in the registry.
   */
Method code:
652 |   FunctionType buildAndRegister() {
653 |     if (returnType == null) {
654 |       // Infer return types.
655 |       // We need to be extremely conservative about this, because of two
656 |       // competing needs.
657 |       // 1) If we infer the return type of f too widely, then we won't be able
658 |       //    to assign f to other functions.
659 |       // 2) If we infer the return type of f too narrowly, then we won't be
660 |       //    able to override f in subclasses.
661 |       // So we only infer in cases where the user doesn't expect to write
662 |       // @return annotations--when it's very obvious that the function returns
663 |       // nothing.
664 |       if (!contents.mayHaveNonEmptyReturns() &&
665 |           !contents.mayHaveSingleThrow() &&
666 |           !contents.mayBeFromExterns()) {
667 |         returnType = typeRegistry.getNativeType(VOID_TYPE);
668 |         returnTypeInferred = true;
669 |       }
670 |     }
671 | 
672 |     if (returnType == null) {
673 |       returnType = typeRegistry.getNativeType(UNKNOWN_TYPE);
674 |     }
675 | 
676 |     if (parametersNode == null) {
677 |       throw new IllegalStateException(
678 |           "All Function types must have params and a return type");
679 |     }
680 | 
681 |     FunctionType fnType;
682 |     if (isConstructor) {
683 |       fnType = getOrCreateConstructor();
684 |     } else if (isInterface) {
685 |       fnType = typeRegistry.createInterfaceType(
686 |           fnName, contents.getSourceNode(), classTemplateTypeNames);
687 |       if (getScopeDeclaredIn().isGlobal() && !fnName.isEmpty()) {
688 |         typeRegistry.declareType(fnName, fnType.getInstanceType());
689 |       }
690 |       maybeSetBaseType(fnType);
691 |     } else {
692 |       fnType = new FunctionBuilder(typeRegistry)
693 |           .withName(fnName)
694 |           .withSourceNode(contents.getSourceNode())
695 |           .withParamsNode(parametersNode)
696 |           .withReturnType(returnType, returnTypeInferred)
697 |           .withTypeOfThis(thisType)
698 |           .withTemplateKeys(templateTypeNames)
699 |           .build();
700 |       maybeSetBaseType(fnType);
701 |     }
702 | 
703 |     if (implementedInterfaces != null) {
704 |       fnType.setImplementedInterfaces(implementedInterfaces);
705 |     }
706 | 
707 |     if (extendedInterfaces != null) {
708 |       fnType.setExtendedInterfaces(extendedInterfaces);
709 |     }
710 | 
711 |     typeRegistry.clearTemplateTypeNames();
712 | 
713 |     return fnType;
714 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.TemplateTypeMap.checkEquivalenceHelper(TemplateTypeMap,EquivalenceMethod)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/rhino/jstype/TemplateTypeMap.java
Original range: 196-243
Documentation:
/**
   * Determines if this map and the specified map have equivalent template
   * types.
   */
Method code:
196 |   public boolean checkEquivalenceHelper(
197 |       TemplateTypeMap that, EquivalenceMethod eqMethod) {
198 |     ImmutableList<TemplateType> thisKeys = getTemplateKeys();
199 |     ImmutableList<TemplateType> thatKeys = that.getTemplateKeys();
200 | 
201 |     EquivalenceMatch[] thatMatches = new EquivalenceMatch[thatKeys.size()];
202 |     Arrays.fill(thatMatches, EquivalenceMatch.NO_KEY_MATCH);
203 | 
204 |     for (int i = 0; i < thisKeys.size(); i++) {
205 |       TemplateType thisKey = thisKeys.get(i);
206 |       JSType thisType = getResolvedTemplateType(thisKey);
207 |       EquivalenceMatch thisMatch = EquivalenceMatch.NO_KEY_MATCH;
208 | 
209 |       for (int j = 0; j < thatKeys.size(); j++) {
210 |         TemplateType thatKey = thatKeys.get(j);
211 |         JSType thatType = that.getResolvedTemplateType(thatKey);
212 | 
213 |         // Cross-compare every key-value pair in this TemplateTypeMap with
214 |         // those in that TemplateTypeMap. Update the Equivalence match for both
215 |         // key-value pairs involved.
216 |         if (thisKey == thatKey) {
217 |           EquivalenceMatch newMatchType = EquivalenceMatch.VALUE_MISMATCH;
218 |           if (thisType.checkEquivalenceHelper(thatType, eqMethod)) {
219 |             newMatchType = EquivalenceMatch.VALUE_MATCH;
220 |           }
221 | 
222 |           if (thisMatch != EquivalenceMatch.VALUE_MATCH) {
223 |             thisMatch = newMatchType;
224 |           }
225 |           if (thatMatches[j] != EquivalenceMatch.VALUE_MATCH) {
226 |             thatMatches[j] = newMatchType;
227 |           }
228 |         }
229 |       }
230 | 
231 |       if (failedEquivalenceCheck(thisMatch, eqMethod)) {
232 |         return false;
233 |       }
234 |     }
235 | 
236 |     for (int i = 0; i < thatMatches.length; i++) {
237 |       if (failedEquivalenceCheck(thatMatches[i], eqMethod)) {
238 |         return false;
239 |       }
240 |     }
241 | 
242 |     return true;
243 |   }

Signature: com.google.javascript.jscomp.parsing.JsDocInfoParser.parseHelperLoop(JsDocToken,List<ExtendedTypeInfo>)
Source: src/com/google/javascript/jscomp/parsing/JsDocInfoParser.java
Original range: 226-271
Documentation:

Method code:
226 |   private boolean parseHelperLoop(JsDocToken token,
227 |                                   List<ExtendedTypeInfo> extendedTypes) {
228 |     while (true) {
229 |       switch (token) {
230 |         case ANNOTATION:
231 |           if (state == State.SEARCHING_ANNOTATION) {
232 |             state = State.SEARCHING_NEWLINE;
233 |             token = parseAnnotation(token, extendedTypes);
234 |           } else {
235 |             token = next();
236 |           }
237 |           break;
238 | 
239 |         case EOC:
240 |           if (hasParsedFileOverviewDocInfo()) {
241 |             fileOverviewJSDocInfo = retrieveAndResetParsedJSDocInfo();
242 |           }
243 |           checkExtendedTypes(extendedTypes);
244 |           return true;
245 | 
246 |         case EOF:
247 |           // discard any accumulated information
248 |           jsdocBuilder.build(null);
249 |           parser.addParserWarning("msg.unexpected.eof",
250 |               stream.getLineno(), stream.getCharno());
251 |           checkExtendedTypes(extendedTypes);
252 |           return false;
253 | 
254 |         case EOL:
255 |           if (state == State.SEARCHING_NEWLINE) {
256 |             state = State.SEARCHING_ANNOTATION;
257 |           }
258 |           token = next();
259 |           break;
260 | 
261 |         default:
262 |           if (token == JsDocToken.STAR && state == State.SEARCHING_ANNOTATION) {
263 |             token = next();
264 |           } else {
265 |             state = State.SEARCHING_NEWLINE;
266 |             token = eatTokensUntilEOL();
267 |           }
268 |           break;
269 |       }
270 |     }
271 |   }
